section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which agency handles driver licensing and permits in Maryland?
options: a:Maryland DMV,b:Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA),c:Maryland DOT,d:Maryland Secretary of State
note: Maryland's Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) handles driver licensing, vehicle registration, and permits. Maryland does not have a traditional DMV — the MVA is the equivalent agency in Maryland.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Maryland's real MVA knowledge test has 25 questions. How many must you answer correctly to pass — and what makes this threshold unusual?
options: a:18 correct (72%) — lower than most states,b:20 correct (80%) — same as most states,c:22 correct (88%) — higher than most states,d:25 correct (100%) — perfect score required
note: Maryland requires 22 out of 25 correct — an 88% passing threshold. This is significantly higher than the 80% standard used by most other states. Maryland's stricter standard means you can miss only 3 questions. This makes thorough preparation especially important.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How many questions can you miss on Maryland's MVA knowledge test and still pass?
options: a:5 questions (80% threshold),b:4 questions (84% threshold),c:3 questions (88% threshold),d:2 questions (92% threshold)
note: You can miss only 3 questions on Maryland's 25-question test. At 88%, Maryland's passing threshold is one of the highest in the nation. If you miss 4 or more questions, you fail. Thorough study of the Maryland Driver's Manual is essential.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum age for a Maryland learner's permit applicant?
options: a:15,b:15 and three-quarters (15¾),c:16,d:14
note: Maryland requires applicants to be at least 15 years and 9 months old (15¾) to apply for a learner's permit. This is a precise age requirement — slightly higher than the typical 15-year minimum used by many other states.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for a Maryland driver age 21 or older?
note: Maryland sets the DUI limit at 0.08% BAC for drivers 21 and older. Maryland also has a separate DWI charge for BAC between 0.07% and 0.08%, which carries penalties but is distinct from DUI. Commercial drivers face a stricter 0.04% limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What BAC triggers Maryland's zero tolerance law for drivers under 21?
note: Maryland sets the underage alcohol limit at 0.02% BAC for drivers under 21. This is the standard zero tolerance threshold used by most states — effectively prohibiting any alcohol consumption before driving for those under 21.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Maryland's GDL program, how many hours of supervised driving must a permit holder complete?
options: a:30 hours (10 at night),b:60 hours (10 at night),c:40 hours (10 at night),d:50 hours (10 at night)
note: Maryland requires 60 hours of supervised driving practice, with at least 10 hours driven at night. The supervising driver must be a licensed driver age 21 or older seated in the front seat. These hours must be certified before applying for a provisional license.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit on Maryland urban streets when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:25 mph,b:30 mph,c:35 mph,d:45 mph
note: Maryland sets the default speed limit in urban and business areas at 30 mph when no sign is posted. On rural roads, the default is 55 mph. Always check for posted signs — but use these defaults when no sign is visible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Maryland's Move Over law requires what when approaching a stationary emergency vehicle with flashing lights on a highway?
options: a:Slow to 25 mph only,b:Move one lane away if safe, or reduce speed to 20 mph below the posted limit if a lane change is not possible,c:Stop completely behind the vehicle,d:Only required for police — not tow trucks
note: Maryland's Move Over law requires moving one lane away from stationary emergency, law enforcement, utility, or tow vehicles with flashing lights. If a safe lane change is not possible, reduce speed to at least 20 mph below the posted speed limit (or 20 mph on roads posted under 40 mph).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You approach a school bus stopped on an undivided road with flashing red lights and stop arm extended. You must:
options: a:Stop only if you are directly behind the bus,b:Stop in both directions at least 20 feet from the bus,c:Slow to 15 mph and pass carefully,d:Stop only if children are visible outside
note: Maryland law requires all vehicles in both directions on an undivided road to stop at least 20 feet from a school bus displaying flashing red lights. Wait until the stop arm retracts and lights stop before proceeding. On a divided highway with a median, only traffic behind the bus must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must Maryland drivers turn on their headlights?
options: a:Only from sunset to sunrise,b:From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and when visibility is under 1,000 feet,c:Only in rain and fog,d:Only at night between 10 PM and 5 AM
note: Maryland requires headlights from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise, and whenever weather reduces visibility to less than 1,000 feet. Maryland's threshold of 1,000 feet is more conservative than many other states, which use 500 feet.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution,b:Yield to cross traffic and proceed,c:Come to a complete stop, yield, and proceed when safe,d:Continue at the posted speed
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign in Maryland. Make a complete stop, yield to all traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when the way is clear. A flashing yellow means caution — reduce speed but a full stop is not required.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum recommended following distance in Maryland under normal conditions?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Maryland recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. In rain, fog, or on wet roads, increase to at least 6 seconds. The 3-second rule: count 3 seconds from when the car ahead passes a fixed point to when you reach the same point.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane road in Maryland, when may you legally cross a solid yellow center line?
options: a:When the road ahead is visible for at least 500 feet,b:You may never cross a solid yellow line on your side to pass,c:When the vehicle ahead is going significantly below the limit,d:When you signal for at least 200 feet in advance
note: A solid yellow line on your side is an absolute prohibition on passing. No exceptions. Only when a dashed (broken) yellow line is on your side may you pass when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Maryland seatbelt law requires which occupants to wear a seatbelt?
options: a:Driver and front-seat passengers only,b:All occupants,c:Only those under 18,d:Driver only
note: Maryland requires all vehicle occupants — in all seating positions — to wear a seatbelt. Maryland has primary enforcement. Children must use appropriate child safety seats based on age and size.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches from behind, you must:
options: a:Accelerate to clear the area,b:Pull to the right edge and stop,c:Slow to 10 mph in your current lane,d:Move to the left lane and slow down
note: Maryland law requires you to immediately pull to the right edge of the road and stop when an emergency vehicle with active lights and siren approaches. Remain stopped until the vehicle passes. If in an intersection, clear it first, then pull over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Can you make a right turn on a red light in Maryland?
options: a:No, right turns on red are prohibited statewide,b:Yes, after a complete stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, unless a sign prohibits it,c:Yes, without stopping if the turn is clear,d:Only on one-way streets
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Maryland after a complete stop, yielding to all pedestrians and cross traffic, and unless a 'No Turn on Red' sign is posted. Always make a full stop — rolling through on red while turning right is illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at exactly the same time as a vehicle to your left. Who goes first?
options: a:The vehicle on your left goes first,b:You go first — yield to the right means the other driver yields to you,c:The larger vehicle goes first,d:Whoever got there first in the sequence goes first
note: At a 4-way stop when vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the right has the right of way. The vehicle on your left must yield to you. This is the universal tie-breaking rule. If you arrived clearly before the other driver, you go first regardless of direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady red arrow traffic signal mean?
options: a:You may turn in the arrow direction if no traffic is present,b:You must stop and may not move in the arrow direction until the signal changes,c:Slow down and turn carefully in the arrow direction,d:The signal is broken — treat as a stop sign
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and may not turn in the indicated direction until the signal changes to green. Unlike a green ball (which allows right turns on red after stopping), a red arrow prohibits movement in that direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the maximum speed limit on Maryland rural interstate highways?
options: a:55 mph,b:60 mph,c:65 mph,d:70 mph
note: Maryland's maximum speed limit on rural interstate highways is 65 mph for passenger vehicles. Some urban sections may have lower posted limits. Maryland's maximum of 65 mph is lower than the 70 mph limit used in many other states.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian is crossing in a marked crosswalk. You must:
options: a:Proceed if you have a green light,b:Slow to 20 mph and proceed carefully,c:Stop and yield until the pedestrian has completely cleared the roadway,d:Yield only if the pedestrian is in your direct lane
note: Maryland law requires stopping and yielding to pedestrians in crosswalks. You must remain stopped until the pedestrian has completely crossed — even if you have a green light. Pedestrian right-of-way in a crosswalk is absolute in Maryland.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Maryland's MVA passing threshold is 88% — how does this compare to most other states?
options: a:It is lower than the national average of 90%,b:It is the same as most states — 80% is the standard,c:It is higher than the 80% standard used by most states — making it harder to pass,d:It is the lowest in the country
note: Maryland's 88% (22/25) passing threshold is significantly higher than the 80% standard used by most other states. This means you can only miss 3 questions — far less room for error than states where you can miss 7 or 8. Thorough preparation of the Maryland Driver's Manual is critical.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Maryland law requires you to signal before a turn or lane change at least how far in advance?
options: a:50 feet,b:100 feet,c:200 feet,d:300 feet
note: Maryland law requires drivers to signal at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes. On higher-speed roads, signaling earlier is advisable. Failing to signal or signaling too late is illegal and dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in fog in Maryland, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beams for maximum range,b:Low beams or fog lights,c:Hazard flashers only,d:No special requirement
note: In fog, use low beams or dedicated fog lights — never high beams. High beams reflect off fog particles and create glare. Maryland's coastal and low-lying areas can experience sudden and dense fog, so this rule is particularly important in those regions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are at a railroad crossing with flashing lights and a lowered gate. What must you do?
options: a:Slow to 15 mph and proceed if you can see no train,b:Stop and wait until the gate rises and lights stop flashing,c:Stop, look, and proceed if you are certain no train is coming,d:Only stop if a sign is present requiring it
note: When a railroad crossing has active warning signals (flashing lights) and/or a lowered gate, stop completely and wait until the gate fully rises and lights stop flashing. Never try to beat a train or drive around a gate — trains cannot stop quickly and are much faster than they appear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: Return to your original lane only after you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed (including its headlights) in your inside rearview mirror and you have checked your blind spot. This ensures you have enough space and do not cut the other driver off.

question: When may you legally drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When warning lights are not flashing.,b:When you can see clearly both directions.,c:Never.,d:When traffic is backed up.
note: You must never drive around or under lowered railroad gates, even if you do not see a train or traffic is delayed. Trains are fast and cannot stop quickly, and signals can activate before you see the train. Always wait until the gates are fully raised and the lights stop flashing.

question: What restriction applies to all drivers under 21 regarding alcohol?
options: a:They cannot drive after consuming any alcohol.,b:They cannot drive after midnight.,c:They cannot smoke while driving.,d:They cannot drive on highways.
note: Drivers under 21 are prohibited from driving after consuming any alcohol; a zero-tolerance rule applies and violations can suspend licenses.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a pedestrian began crossing after the Don't Walk started and is in the intersection when your light turns green, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,b:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before going.,c:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,d:Honk and continue carefully.
note: You must yield to pedestrians already in the intersection and wait until they have crossed before proceeding on your green signal.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.,b:Put on cruise control.,c:Slow down.,d:Speed up to maintain momentum.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when your tires ride on a layer of water and lose contact with the road, causing loss of steering and braking control. The best way to reduce this risk is to slow down in wet conditions and drive smoothly, especially in heavy rain or standing water.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a green light but the intersection is blocked by traffic, what is the best action?
options: a:Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.,b:Don't enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,c:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can completely clear it, even if the light is green. Entering and stopping in the middle of the intersection can block cross traffic and emergency vehicles and may be illegal. Wait behind the stop line until there is enough space to drive all the way through.

question: Regulatory signs are typically what color?
options: a:Yellow.,b:White.,c:Green.,d:Red.
note: Most regulatory signs that tell you about laws and rules (such as speed limits, lane use, and parking) are white rectangles with black or red lettering or symbols. Some specific regulatory signs, like STOP and DO NOT ENTER, are red, but the general background color for many regulatory signs is white.

question: If you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in your lane and slow down.,b:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,c:Drive to the right edge and slow down but stay moving.,d:Speed up and get out of the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches from behind, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over and stop.

question: If you must park in an unusual area, what should you do to reduce hazard?
options: a:Park with your reverse lights on.,b:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,c:Park five feet from the curb.
note: If you must park in an unusual or less visible area, your main goal is to avoid creating a hazard. Choose a location where your vehicle can be clearly seen by drivers approaching from any direction, and use hazard lights if appropriate and legal so others can spot your parked vehicle in time to react safely.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) rises, what happens to you?
options: a:More sober.,b:More coordinated.,c:More intoxicated.
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream. As BAC increases, your judgment, reaction time, coordination, and vision become more impaired. A higher BAC always means you are more intoxicated and less able to drive safely.

question: If it feels like your tires have lost contact with the road surface (hydroplaning), what should you do?
options: a:Ease your foot off the gas and avoid braking.,b:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.,c:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,d:Steer sharply to the side of the road.
note: When your vehicle hydroplanes, the tires ride on top of the water and lose grip with the road. Any sudden braking, accelerating, or sharp steering can cause a skid. The safest response is to gently ease your foot off the accelerator, keep the steering wheel straight, and wait until you feel the tires regain traction before braking or turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,b:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, you need enough space before moving back into the right lane so you do not cut off the other driver. A common safe rule is to wait until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror. This indicates you have created a safe following distance before returning to the lane.

question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from your system?
options: a:Drink strong coffee.,b:Wait.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Time is the only factor that reduces BAC; eating, coffee, or showers do not speed up alcohol elimination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what circumstances may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:If you entered the intersection on a green light.,b:During rush hour traffic.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You should not enter an intersection unless there is enough space to clear it completely, even if the light is green. Stopping in the middle of the intersection blocks cross traffic and can create serious safety hazards. The only time a vehicle may be in the intersection when the light changes is when it entered lawfully and is completing a turn or clearing the intersection, not sitting and blocking it due to congestion.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat an intersection controlled by a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Treat it like a stop sign—come to a complete stop, yield, then proceed.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped while the light is red.,d:Treat it the same as a flashing yellow signal.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then look for other vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians. Proceed only when the way is clear and it is your turn to go.

question: What should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Activate your turn signal.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Brake hard.
note: Reducing speed before entering a curve helps you maintain better control and traction. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control, especially in poor conditions. Slow to a safe speed before you begin turning, then steer smoothly through the curve.

question: Where should a driver be watching while driving?
options: a:Only directly ahead.,b:Beside, ahead, and behind the vehicle.,c:Only in mirrors.,d:At dashboard instruments.
note: Safe drivers constantly scan the entire traffic scene: ahead for developing hazards, to the sides for pedestrians and cross traffic, and behind using mirrors to know what other vehicles are doing. This wide scanning helps you anticipate problems early and react smoothly instead of making sudden moves.

question: What type of information do blue traffic signs provide?
options: a:Motorist services such as rest areas or hospitals.,b:Construction and maintenance warnings.,c:Mileage to specific locations.
note: Blue traffic signs are used for motorist services and information, such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals. Construction and maintenance warnings are orange, and mileage or destination information is usually shown on green guide signs.

question: Which headlights are best to use when driving in fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers.,c:Fog lights only.,d:Low beam headlights.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, use low beam headlights because their light aims down toward the road and reduces glare. High beams reflect off moisture droplets in the air and can bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see. If your vehicle has fog lights, you may use them together with low beams for better visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about using a deceleration lane to exit is true?
options: a:Do not use your turn signal until the vehicle has moved into the deceleration lane.,b:Do not follow the posted warning speeds unless the roadway is slippery.,c:Do not slow down until your vehicle has moved into the deceleration lane.
note: Use your turn signal before entering the deceleration lane to show others you are exiting. Stay at normal highway speed on the main roadway, then move into the deceleration lane and begin slowing down there. This keeps through traffic flowing smoothly and reduces the risk of rear-end collisions on the main lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On the interstate, what is the best way to avoid traffic merging from on-ramps to your right?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position.,b:Slow down.,c:Change lanes to the left when it is safe.
note: On interstates, traffic often enters from the right. When you see vehicles merging, the safest and most courteous action is to move one lane to the left if it is legal and safe. This creates space for merging vehicles and reduces sudden braking or lane changes. If you cannot move left safely, adjust your speed slightly to help them merge smoothly.

question: When another vehicle is passing you, what is the proper action?
options: a:Brake hard.,b:Maintain a constant speed.,c:Speed up.
note: When another vehicle is passing you, you should maintain a steady speed or slow slightly so the pass can be completed quickly and safely. Do not speed up, because that forces the passing driver to stay in the oncoming lane longer and increases the risk of a collision. Hard braking is also unsafe unless needed to avoid a crash, because it can surprise drivers behind you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If motorists see pedestrians in an upcoming crosswalk, what should they do?
options: a:Pull to the right and go around.,b:Wait for the pedestrians to cross.,c:Proceed since the motorist has right-of-way.,d:Honk to hurry them along.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk and in many states at unmarked crosswalks as well. If you see pedestrians in or about to enter the crosswalk, slow down and stop, then wait until they have completely crossed your lane and it is safe before proceeding. Going around them or trying to hurry them with your horn is dangerous and illegal.

question: What is the only proven method to remove alcohol from your system?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Give your body time.,c:Take a cold shower.,d:Exercise vigorously.
note: Only time allows your body to process and eliminate alcohol. Your liver can handle only a certain amount per hour, and nothing speeds this up. Coffee, cold showers, or exercise might make you feel more awake, but they do not lower your blood alcohol concentration or make you safe to drive.

question: If you begin to feel drowsy while driving, what is the safest action?
options: a:Open a window.,b:Stop and either rest or switch drivers.,c:Drink something with caffeine.
note: To avoid fatigued driving, stop frequently during long trips and rest or change drivers to ensure you are alert.

question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:If there isn't room on the other side to fully clear the tracks.,b:When the crossing is in a busy town.,c:Only if a train is visible.,d:If you are carrying no passengers.
note: You must never enter a railroad crossing unless there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks. If you move forward without enough room, you risk being trapped on the tracks if traffic stops. Always wait behind the stop line or before the tracks until you can drive completely across without stopping.

question: What should you remember when driving on gravel or dirt roads?
options: a:Visibility is better than on pavement.,b:Your tires have less traction than on pavement, so you must slow down.,c:Your tires grip the road better than on pavement.
note: On gravel or dirt, the loose surface greatly reduces traction compared with paved roads. Your tires can slide more easily, especially when braking or turning. You should slow down, increase following distance, and make all steering, braking, and acceleration smooth to avoid skids.

question: Which of the following removes alcohol and its effects from your body?
options: a:Drinking caffeine.,b:Eating foods high in fat.,c:Time.
note: Only time allows the body to eliminate alcohol and reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC). No food, drink, or activity will speed this process.

question: What is a likely result of continuous hard braking on ice or snow?
options: a:Helps you stop faster.,b:Locks the front wheels and causes loss of steering.,c:Keeps the brakes from freezing.
note: On ice or snow, hard continuous braking can cause your wheels to lock, especially the front wheels, which results in a loss of steering control. Instead, slow down early and brake gently. If your vehicle has ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and let the system pump the brakes for you while you steer.

question: On a slippery road, how should you adjust your following distance?
options: a:No different than normal.,b:Farther than normal.,c:Closer than normal.,d:Only if it's snowing.
note: On slippery roads, it takes much longer to stop, so you must increase your following distance. Leaving more space gives you extra time to brake gently and avoid skidding if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,b:Move into another lane while within an intersection.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: You should never change lanes while you are actually in an intersection. Intersections are busy areas where vehicles, pedestrians, and turning traffic may move unpredictably. Lane changes there increase the risk of side collisions. Instead, change lanes before or after the intersection, and always check mirrors, blind spots, and signal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red light with a green arrow, when may you proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:You first come to a complete stop.,b:You wait until the light changes.,c:You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.
note: A green arrow is a protected turn signal for the lane it controls. If you are in that lane, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow when the roadway is clear, but you must still yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any traffic already in the intersection.

question: In very foggy conditions, what lighting should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Emergency flashers.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Parking lights only.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights (and fog lights if your vehicle has them). High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back at you, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and reduce glare so you can better see lane lines and the edge of the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway, how fast should you be driving?
options: a:Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.,b:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,c:At the posted speed limit for freeway traffic.,d:As slow as needed to enter safely.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed at or near that of traffic already on the freeway, as long as it is safe. Matching the flow of traffic makes it easier to find a gap and reduces the risk of collisions caused by large speed differences.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk, may you pass it?
options: a:You may not pass that vehicle.,b:You may go around if it seems safe.,c:You must honk first.,d:You may pass on the left only.
note: You must never pass a vehicle that is stopped at a crosswalk. That driver may be yielding to pedestrians you cannot see from your position. Passing could put those pedestrians directly in your path and cause a serious collision. Stay behind the stopped vehicle until you are sure the crosswalk is clear and traffic can proceed.

question: If there are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked cars to your right, where should you steer?
options: a:Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,b:Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.,c:Take a middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
note: When you have hazards on both sides—oncoming traffic to the left and parked cars to the right—you should steer a middle course. This gives you space from oncoming vehicles while also reducing the risk of hitting parked cars or an opening door. Adjust slightly as needed, but avoid driving too close to either side.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also plan to turn right, how should you act?
options: a:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.,b:Quickly turn before the truck or bus is able to.,c:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.
note: Large vehicles may swing wide during turns; do not try to pass between the truck and curb—wait until it completes the turn.

question: What is the primary danger of excessive speed?
options: a:Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.,b:Helps you maneuver around obstacles.,c:Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.
note: Driving too fast increases your stopping distance and reduces the time you have to react. If a crash happens at higher speed, the impact forces are much greater, which makes serious injury or death more likely. Speeding does not significantly reduce travel time on most trips but greatly increases crash risk and severity.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs traffic to go through a red signal, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the light turns green.,b:Follow the officer's directions and go through the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.
note: A police officer directing traffic has authority over traffic signals and signs. If an officer tells you to go through a red light, you must follow the officer’s directions, proceeding carefully as instructed. Their job is to manage traffic safely in special situations such as crashes, road work, or signal malfunctions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or attempting to pass, what must you do?
options: a:Check your blind spots and mirrors.,b:Signal your intention before changing lanes.,c:All of the above.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, you must signal to let other drivers know your intentions and check that the lane is clear. Use your mirrors and also turn your head to check blind spots that mirrors do not show. Only move into the new lane when you are sure it is safe.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.,b:Slow down gradually and avoid braking heavily.,c:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, ease your foot off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking, because it can cause loss of control, especially with a flat tire. Once you have slowed and the vehicle is stable, brake gently if needed and steer off the road to a safe place.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what checks should you perform to ensure it is safe?
options: a:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder.,b:Check only the inside rearview mirror.,c:Slow down before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This head check lets you see into your blind spot, where vehicles may not appear in your mirrors. Only move when the lane is clear and you have signaled in advance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful regarding passing?
options: a:Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.,b:Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.,c:Both of the above.
note: Passing is illegal in marked no‑passing zones and at railroad crossings in all states. These areas are designed to protect you where visibility or conditions make passing unsafe. You must stay in your lane and wait until you are past the no‑passing zone or crossing before attempting to pass.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:Decrease as a vehicle's speed increases.,b:Are not affected by a vehicle's speed.,c:Increase as a vehicle's speed increases.
note: As speed increases, both your stopping distance and the force of any crash increase. You need more distance to see a hazard, react, and bring the vehicle to a complete stop. In a collision, higher speed means much greater impact energy, which leads to more severe damage and injuries.

question: Why is extra road space needed in front of a large truck?
options: a:So other drivers can merge in front.,b:So the truck driver has room to stop.,c:Because the truck travels slower downhill.,d:To allow the truck to change lanes freely.
note: Large trucks are heavy and need much more distance to stop than smaller vehicles. Leaving extra space in front of a truck gives the driver enough room to brake safely if traffic slows or stops suddenly, reducing the risk of rear‑end collisions.

question: Which behavior is a likely sign of an aggressive driver?
options: a:The number of passengers in their car.,b:Their erratic and improper lane changes.,c:Their tendency to drive slowly.
note: Erratic, improper lane changes are a classic sign of aggressive driving. Aggressive drivers often weave through traffic, change lanes without signaling, cut others off, or follow too closely. When you see this behavior, stay calm, give them space, and avoid eye contact or confrontation.

question: Why is nighttime driving more hazardous than daytime driving?
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night.
note: Night driving is more hazardous mainly because you cannot see as far ahead. Headlights provide limited range, reduce your ability to spot hazards early, and glare from oncoming lights can further reduce visibility. Even if you feel alert, you must slow down and increase following distance at night to compensate for reduced visibility.

question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, how must you respond?
options: a:Drive around if no train is visible.,b:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates and wait.,c:Slowly creep under the gates.,d:Proceed if you see only one rail track.
note: When gates are down and lights are flashing at a railroad crossing, you must stop and wait. It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around or under the gates, even if you do not see a train. Trains are fast, heavy, and cannot stop quickly, so you must remain stopped until the gates are fully raised and the lights stop flashing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.,c:After signaling for one second.,d:As soon as you pass the front bumper.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your lane until you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror, including its headlights in the case of a car at night. This ensures you have left enough space and will not cut the other driver off when you return to your lane.

question: If a driver is tailgating you on a two-lane road and there is no lane to move into, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to pass.,b:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.,c:Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.
note: If someone is tailgating and you cannot move to another lane, gradually reduce your speed to encourage them to pass when it is safe. Do not speed up or brake suddenly, as that can increase the risk of a rear-end collision. Smoothly creating more space in front of you gives you more time to react and reduces the danger from the tailgater behind.

question: What is the best general strategy to avoid dangerous driving situations?
options: a:Always keep your eyes focused ahead of your car.,b:Turn off the radio.,c:Know what is happening around your vehicle.
note: Constantly checking mirrors and scanning ahead and to the sides helps you spot hazards early, such as sudden stops, merging vehicles, or pedestrians. Knowing what is happening all around your vehicle gives you more time and space to react safely and avoid dangerous situations.

question: If you see a lane sign showing an arrow with the word 'ONLY' underneath, what must you do?
options: a:Always make a lane change.,b:Look for a destination sign to follow.,c:Travel in the direction of the arrow.
note: A lane control sign with an arrow and the word “ONLY” means traffic in that lane must go in the direction of the arrow and cannot turn or continue straight in any other direction. You must follow the arrow shown when you are in that lane.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. Passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line, and drivers on the side with the solid line must not cross it to pass.

question: When may you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.,b:When the yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.,c:If the yellow line on the opposite side is broken.
note: For two-way roads with a solid and a broken yellow line together, you may only cross to pass when the line closest to your lane is broken and it is safe. If the line next to you is solid, you must not cross it to pass, even if the other side has a broken line.

question: What is a possible effect of taking a prescription drug while drinking alcohol?
options: a:There will likely be no effect.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:It can make you unfit to drive.
note: Many prescription drugs can cause drowsiness, slowed reaction time, or poor judgment. When combined with alcohol, these effects are often stronger, making you unsafe to drive and potentially putting you over the legal limit or otherwise unfit to operate a vehicle.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate about passing?
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means no passing is allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe, but you may not use the opposing lane to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only when:
options: a:You increase your speed before the turn.,b:Traffic on the street moves to the right.,c:Traffic on the street moves to the left.
note: On a one‑way street, you may turn left onto another one‑way street only if traffic on the street you are turning onto flows to the left and there is no sign prohibiting the turn. Always yield to pedestrians and other traffic and complete the turn into the nearest left lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, whom must you yield to?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Only oncoming vehicles.,c:No one, you have the right-of-way.,d:Only vehicles on your right.
note: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians crossing the street you are turning into. Wait until there is a safe gap in oncoming traffic and the crosswalk is clear before completing your turn.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,b:Only if the traffic lights favor the pedestrian.,c:You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian and be prepared to yield whenever necessary to prevent a collision.
note: Drivers must do everything reasonably possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even if the pedestrian is acting unsafely. You must always be prepared to yield to pedestrians in crosswalks (marked or unmarked) and at intersections, and you should slow or stop whenever necessary to prevent a collision, even if you technically have the right‑of‑way.

question: What do 'No passing zone' signs indicate to drivers?
options: a:To speed up slightly.,b:That it is not safe to pass.,c:To maintain a steady speed.
note: A No Passing Zone sign tells you that passing is prohibited because it is unsafe, such as near hills, curves, intersections, or where visibility is limited. You must stay in your lane and not drive into the oncoming lane to pass another vehicle in this area.

question: What should you do when the roadway is wet or icy?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed.,b:Speed up.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: On wet, snowy, or icy roads, your tires have less traction, so it takes longer to stop and is easier to lose control. You should reduce your speed and drive smoothly, avoiding sudden braking or sharp steering.

question: When must drivers yield right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.,b:Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.,c:Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks whenever they are crossing or about to cross in the driver’s lane or an adjacent lane.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians who are in a marked or unmarked crosswalk at an intersection. You must slow or stop as needed to let them cross safely, regardless of whether they signal you or what they are doing.

question: What risk does fatigue pose while driving?
options: a:Missing an exit.,b:Being late for an appointment.,c:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
note: Fatigue slows your reaction time, reduces your ability to notice hazards, and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel. Even brief “microsleeps” can lead to losing control of the vehicle and serious crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to drive faster than the posted speed limit?
options: a:Never.,b:If you feel it is reasonable and prudent.,c:When passing another vehicle.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum speed allowed under ideal conditions. It is never legal to exceed that limit, and you must often drive slower when conditions such as traffic, weather, or road surface require it for safety.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, what must a driver do?
options: a:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right-of-way, and proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe.

question: On a green arrow signal, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.,b:Wait four seconds before turning.,c:Only yield to vehicles.,d:Turn immediately without checking.
note: A green arrow permits the turn but requires yielding to any vehicles, cyclists, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

question: When should you allow extra following distance behind another vehicle?
options: a:When following a station wagon.,b:When following a large vehicle, bus, or vehicle towing a trailer that blocks the driver’s rear view.,c:When following a small passenger car.
note: Increase your following distance behind large vehicles, buses, trucks, or vehicles towing trailers because their drivers cannot see directly behind them and they need more space to stop or maneuver. Extra space gives you more time to react if they slow, stop, or make wide turns.

question: If your vehicle has ABS and you must stop on snow or ice, what should you do with the brake pedal?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.
note: With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and keep steady pressure on it. The system automatically pumps the brakes to prevent wheel lockup and help you maintain steering control, even on snow or ice.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal status of texting while driving?
options: a:Permitted if driving at a slow speed.,b:Not legal in most states and highly dangerous.,c:Legal if the driver is 21 years of age or older.
note: Texting while driving is illegal and considered highly distracting; Maryland law prohibits using handheld devices while driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but the intersection is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Turn left and find another route.,b:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,c:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space to clear it completely, even if the light is green. If traffic ahead is stopped, wait behind the crosswalk or stop line until you can drive all the way through without blocking the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.,b:It notifies other drivers of your intended actions.,c:It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.
note: Signaling throughout a turn lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians know exactly what you plan to do, reducing surprises and collisions. You should keep your signal on before and during the turn so others can react safely.

question: Where are large trucks' blind spots commonly located?
options: a:On the immediate left of the cab.,b:Directly behind the body.,c:Both on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the body.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots, often called "no-zones," where the driver cannot see you. A major blind spot is directly behind the trailer, and another is along the left side near and behind the cab. If you cannot see the truck driver in their side mirror, they likely cannot see you, so avoid lingering in these areas.

question: Which statement about blind spots is accurate?
options: a:They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side of the vehicle.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirrors.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger cars, so you should give them extra space and avoid driving alongside or close behind them where the driver cannot see you.

question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?
options: a:Drivers must come to a full stop and may not proceed in the arrow's direction.,b:Drivers may turn after stopping.,c:Drivers should speed up to clear the intersection.,d:Drivers may turn if clear.
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and you are not allowed to go in the direction the arrow points until it turns green. Treat it like a red light specifically for that turning movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement is true about driving too slowly on highways?
options: a:Driving too slowly is not an unsafe practice.,b:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,c:The speed at which you drive a vehicle does not affect safety.
note: Driving much slower than surrounding traffic can be dangerous because it causes other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly and may lead to risky passing. On highways, you should generally drive at the posted speed and with the flow of traffic, as long as conditions are safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection with a steady yellow light and haven't entered it, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Come to a safe stop if you can.,c:Drive through regardless.,d:Stop in the middle of the intersection.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you should slow down and stop if you can do so safely. Only continue through if you are too close to the intersection to stop without braking hard or risking a rear-end collision.

question: What is the purpose of broken yellow lines on streets and highways?
options: a:Indicate no passing zones.,b:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line also means you may pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal to do so, but you must watch carefully for oncoming traffic.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?
options: a:Switch to high beams.,b:Turn your lights on and off.,c:Look toward the right edge of the road.,d:Close your eyes briefly.
note: When oncoming headlights are too bright, avoid looking directly at them. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane markings as a guide. This reduces glare while helping you keep your vehicle in the correct position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You enter a left-turn lane and there is oncoming traffic. What should you do before turning?
options: a:Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.,b:Signal at least 100 feet before the intersection and keep your wheels straight while waiting.,c:Move to the left of the center lane.
note: Before making a left turn, signal well in advance—typically at least 100 feet before the turn in most areas—so other drivers know your intentions. As you wait to turn, keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead. If your wheels are turned left and you are hit from behind, your vehicle could be pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Emergency flashers only.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low-beam headlights.
note: When dust, smoke, or similar conditions reduce visibility, turn on your low-beam headlights so you can see and be seen by others. High beams can reflect off particles in the air and make it harder to see, while parking lights or emergency flashers alone do not provide adequate forward lighting or make your vehicle clearly visible at a distance.

question: How should you react to a flashing yellow light at an intersection?
options: a:Stop, then proceed when clear.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Yield to all traffic before crossing.,d:Ignore it and go normally.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down, look carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: What does the acronym BAC stand for?
options: a:Blood alcohol concentration.,b:Big alcohol content.,c:Blood alcohol conservation.
note: BAC measures the percentage of alcohol in a person's bloodstream; 0.08% or higher is the legal limit for drivers 21 and older.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle approaching with flashing lights, how must you respond?
options: a:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.,b:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until it has passed.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it has passed.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and/or a siren, you must pull as close as you safely can to the right edge of the road and stop, waiting until the vehicle has passed before reentering traffic.

question: A broken yellow centerline next to your lane indicates what about passing?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline next to your lane means you may cross it to pass a vehicle ahead of you on the left, but only when the lane is clear and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the safest course of action?
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly.,b:Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.,c:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the travel lane.
note: If a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, do not brake hard, ease off the accelerator to slow down gradually, and then steer to a safe place out of the traffic lane before stopping.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line on your side is broken, you may cross it to pass another vehicle on the left if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe. You must still judge carefully for enough clear distance and never pass where visibility or conditions make it unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter the roadway from an alley, driveway, or parking lot, what must a driver do?
options: a:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,b:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.,c:Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield the right-of-way.,d:Sound your horn and proceed slowly.
note: When you are coming from an alley, driveway, or parking lot and must cross a sidewalk to enter the street, you must stop before driving across the sidewalk area. Pedestrians on the sidewalk have the right‑of‑way, and you must yield to them and to traffic on the roadway before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a traffic signal that is flashing yellow?
options: a:Maintain your normal speed.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow signal means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you should reduce speed, scan carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, or hazards, and be prepared to yield if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Right, toward the side of the road,c:Left, toward the center of the road
note: When parking downhill on a two‑way road with no curb, turn your front wheels to the right, toward the edge of the road or shoulder. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway instead of into traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive simultaneously from the right and left, to whom should you yield?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), if two vehicles arrive at about the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. Yielding to the vehicle on your right helps prevent confusion and collisions.

question: When changing lanes, what visual check is required?
options: a:Rely on the rearview mirror.,b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Rely on the left side mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. This shoulder check lets you see the blind spot that mirrors cannot cover, helping you avoid vehicles that may be alongside you.

question: If there is a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline, what does it mean?
options: a:Do not pass.,b:Traffic light ahead.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you must not pass other vehicles from your lane. It marks a no‑passing zone because visibility or road conditions make passing unsafe.

question: What should you do to reduce the risk of hydroplaning in rainy conditions?
options: a:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,b:Move to the shoulder of the road as soon as it starts to rain.,c:Decrease your speed.
note: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning, slow down in wet conditions and drive smoothly. Lower speeds help your tires maintain contact with the road instead of riding up on a layer of water, which can cause a complete loss of steering and braking control.

question: Any amount of alcohol in your bloodstream can impair which of the following?
options: a:Knowledge.,b:Right-of-way privileges.,c:Judgment and physical coordination.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect the parts of your brain that control judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Even if you are below the legal limit, your ability to drive safely can be reduced, increasing your risk of a crash and possible legal consequences.

question: How should you respond to a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane?
options: a:You must tell them where to cross the street.,b:You must always yield the right-of-way.,c:You only have to yield if you are at a corner.
note: Pedestrians using a guide dog or carrying a white cane are visually impaired and must always be given the right‑of‑way. Slow down or stop as needed and allow them to cross safely without honking or pressuring them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause a conflict.,b:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,c:Slow down but never stop.
note: At a yield sign you must slow down and be ready to stop. You must let cross or merging traffic go first if they are close enough to be a hazard. Only proceed when you are sure you can enter or cross without interfering with other road users.

question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means which vehicles may pass?
options: a:Driving in both directions may pass.,b:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.,c:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.
note: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic next to the broken line, and not allowed for traffic next to the solid line. Drivers may cross the broken line to pass when it is safe and legal, but must not cross the solid line to pass.

question: What attitude should you have when driving in a construction zone?
options: a:Slightly increase your speed.,b:Expect the unexpected.,c:Expect workers to yield to motorists.
note: In construction zones you should slow down, stay alert, and expect the unexpected. Lanes may shift, workers and equipment may be close to traffic, and traffic may stop suddenly. A cautious, patient attitude helps protect both workers and drivers.

question: What message will be displayed on a red octagon-shaped sign?
options: a:Do not enter.,b:Stop.,c:One-way.
note: A red octagon-shaped sign always means STOP. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to any pedestrians or vehicles with the right-of-way.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, what is the best action for you to take?
options: a:Turn on your high beams to signal them.,b:Look toward the right side of the road.,c:Look toward the center of the roadway.,d:Keep looking straight ahead.
note: If an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly at the glare. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane line as a guide while still checking traffic ahead. This reduces temporary blindness and helps you maintain safe lane position.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you expect?
options: a:The child to be fully in control.,b:The unexpected from the child.,c:That honking will correct behavior.,d:That the child will always stop at intersections.
note: Children on bicycles are often unpredictable. They may suddenly swerve, stop, or enter your lane without warning. You should slow down, give them extra space, and be prepared for unexpected movements rather than assuming they are fully in control or that honking will correct their behavior.

question: When should you increase the space between your vehicle and the one ahead?
options: a:When you are following a small passenger vehicle.,b:When you are being tailgated by another driver.,c:When you are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.
note: If another driver is following you too closely (tailgating), you should increase the space in front of your vehicle. A larger following distance gives you more time to brake gently and reduces the chance that a sudden stop will cause the tailgater to hit you from behind.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How do you know it's safe to return to your lane after passing another car?
options: a:If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.,b:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.,c:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, it is generally safe to return to your lane when you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space ahead of that vehicle. Always signal and check your mirrors and blind spot before moving back into the lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.,b:At a red traffic light.,c:Both of the above.,d:Only at stop signs.
note: You must stop when directed by a police officer and at red traffic lights. Traffic officers’ directions must always be obeyed, even if they differ from signs or signals. You are also required to stop at stop signs and certain other situations, but this question focuses on officers’ orders and red lights together.

question: Before starting the engine, which safety action should you take?
options: a:Buckle your safety belt.,b:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c:Both of the above.
note: Before starting the engine, you should always fasten your own seat belt and make sure all passengers are buckled. This habit ensures everyone is properly restrained before the vehicle moves, greatly reducing the risk of injury in a crash or sudden stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive at the posted maximum speed limit?
options: a:At night.,b:Only under ideal conditions.,c:During rain.,d:Whenever the driver wants.
note: The posted maximum speed is the fastest you may drive only when conditions are ideal: good visibility, dry pavement, light traffic, and safe road conditions. In rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor road conditions, you must drive slower than the posted maximum so you can stop safely and maintain control.

question: Like drugs or alcohol, what effect can drowsiness have on driving?
options: a:Improve awareness.,b:Make you feel better.,c:Impair your judgment.,d:Increase reaction speed.
note: Drowsiness slows your reaction time, narrows your attention, and makes your judgment less reliable, much like alcohol or drugs. A drowsy driver may not notice hazards in time or may make poor decisions, greatly increasing crash risk.

question: How can you keep track of traffic behind you?
options: a:Turn and look out your back window.,b:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,c:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.,d:All of the above.
note: To stay aware of traffic behind you, glance frequently in your mirrors, especially the inside rearview mirror. This helps you notice vehicles that are following too closely, changing lanes, or approaching quickly so you can adjust your driving safely.

question: If the rear of your vehicle skids left, how should you steer to correct it?
options: a:Do not turn your steering wheel.,b:Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.,c:Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.,d:Brake hard and hold the pedal down.
note: In a rear-wheel skid, always steer in the direction the rear of the vehicle is sliding. If the rear skids left, you steer left; if it skids right, you steer right. This helps the vehicle straighten out and regain traction. Avoid sudden braking or overcorrecting, which can make the skid worse.

question: To help others see you as daylight fades, what lights should you use?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Emergency flashers.,d:High beam headlights.
note: As daylight fades or in low-visibility conditions, you should turn on your low beam headlights so others can see you and you can see the road. Parking lights and emergency flashers are not for normal driving, and high beams can blind oncoming drivers or those ahead of you.

question: If you approach a stopped emergency vehicle using visual signals, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed to get around the incident quickly.,b:Ask the emergency workers if they need your help.,c:Move into the lane farthest from the vehicle or slow down.
note: If an emergency vehicle is stopped with visual signals, move over to a non-adjacent lane if possible; otherwise slow down to a safe speed and be prepared to stop.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:They do not have the same physical reflexes as adults.,b:They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults.,c:Both of the above.
note: Children on bicycles are less predictable and often lack the judgment and physical control that adults have. They are also smaller and can be harder to see, especially near parked cars or at driveways. Because of this, you should slow down and give them extra space, particularly near schools, parks, and in residential neighborhoods.

question: If you've had several beers, how can the alcohol effects be reduced?
options: a:Drinking several cups of coffee.,b:Waiting several hours.,c:Taking a cold shower.
note: Once alcohol is in your system, only time can lower your blood alcohol concentration. Coffee, cold showers, exercise, or other “quick fixes” may make you feel more awake but do not make you less impaired. Waiting long enough for your body to process the alcohol is the only safe way to reduce its effects before driving.

question: If a stopped school bus ahead in your lane has red lights flashing, how long must you remain stopped?
options: a:Stop and proceed when you think all of the children have exited the bus.,b:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,c:Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.
note: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped in most situations, whether you are approaching from behind or from the opposite direction on an undivided road. You may not proceed until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, indicating that children are no longer boarding or exiting.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn from a one-way street, which lane should you be in?
options: a:The lane nearest the center of the street.,b:The lane nearest the right curb.,c:The lane nearest the left curb.,d:Any lane as long as it is clear.
note: For a left turn from a one‑way street, you should be in the lane nearest the left curb before turning. Start the turn from that leftmost lane and turn into the first legal lane going in your new direction. Positioning yourself correctly before the turn helps prevent conflicts with other vehicles and keeps your path predictable.

question: Why use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,b:To keep your engine warm.,c:So others can see your vehicle.
note: Headlights help other drivers see you in rain, snow, or fog and also improve your own visibility. Many states require headlights whenever wipers are in continuous use, and you should use low beams in these conditions so you do not create glare.

question: Why is slowing down to look at crashes or odd events discouraged?
options: a:It causes traffic congestion.,b:It prevents rear-end collisions.,c:It improves traffic flow.,d:It helps emergency responders.
note: Slowing down just to look at a crash or unusual event (rubbernecking) disrupts normal traffic flow, creates sudden slowdowns, and increases the risk of rear‑end and other collisions. Keep your attention on the road ahead and maintain a safe, steady speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you check a blind spot when changing lanes?
options: a:Using the inside rearview mirror.,b:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using your side mirror.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; there are areas called blind spots. Before changing lanes, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Wait for the green light before proceeding.,b:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,c:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. Slow down, look for cross traffic and pedestrians, and continue through the intersection only when it is safe to do so; you are not required to stop unless needed for safety.

question: If you approach a steady yellow traffic signal and have not entered the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection and can stop safely, you must come to a stop before the intersection or crosswalk instead of speeding up to beat the red.

question: In fog, rain, or snow which headlights are appropriate to use?
options: a:Low beams.,b:High beams.,c:Fog lights only.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. If your vehicle has fog lights, you may use them in addition to low beams when conditions are very poor, but never rely on fog lights alone.

question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, how should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,c:Leave the front wheels straight.
note: When parking facing uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and let the vehicle roll back slightly until the tire gently touches the curb. This way, if the brakes fail, the curb will stop the vehicle from rolling into traffic.

question: Which type of roadway is most likely to be icy in cold weather after precipitation?
options: a:A hilly, open road,b:A residential road,c:A road in a shaded area.
note: Roads in shaded areas are often the iciest because they receive less sunlight. They freeze sooner and thaw later than open areas, so after snow or rain in cold weather, shaded spots can stay icy even when the rest of the road looks clear.

question: If you see pedestrians near the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:Slow down and pass with caution.
note: When pedestrians are near the roadway, slow down, be prepared to stop, and pass with great caution. People can step into the road unexpectedly, and drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and avoid endangering anyone on or near the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you make room for cars entering the freeway?
options: a:Maintaining your speed and position.,b:Merging into a different lane when possible.,c:Slowing down only if someone honks at you.
note: To help vehicles enter a freeway smoothly, move over to another lane when it is safe so they have space to merge. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to create a safe gap. Maintaining speed without adjusting or waiting for a horn can create dangerous merging situations.

question: How are stopping distances and crash severity affected by higher speeds?
options: a:Are not affected by vehicle speed.,b:Decrease as vehicle speed increases.,c:Increase as vehicle speed increases.
note: Stopping distance and crash severity both increase as speed increases. At higher speeds, your vehicle travels farther during your reaction time and also needs more distance to brake to a stop. In a crash, more speed means more energy to be absorbed, which greatly increases the chance of serious injury or death.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the driver ahead stops at a crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and wait until pedestrians have cleared.,b:Cautiously pass at 10 mph.,c:Change lanes and pass immediately.,d:Honk and go around them.
note: If the driver ahead has stopped at a crosswalk, you must also stop and wait until you are sure pedestrians have cleared. Passing a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk is dangerous and illegal in many states because pedestrians may be crossing where you cannot see them until you stop.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous?
options: a:The speed limit is increased at night.,b:There are fewer cars on the roads at night.,c:Distance and vehicle speed are difficult to judge in the dark.
note: Night driving is more hazardous mainly because you cannot see as far or as clearly. Headlights limit how much of the road you can see, and glare and darkness make it harder to judge other vehicles’ distance and speed. This reduced visibility means you must drive more cautiously at night.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When facing a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Proceed since you have the green.,c:Sound your horn and continue.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection first.
note: A green light means you may go only if the intersection is clear and it is safe. Pedestrians already in the crosswalk have the right-of-way, even when you have a green signal. You must wait until they have safely crossed before you proceed.

question: When passing a motorcycle, what must you ensure?
options: a:Have your vehicle fully in the left lane before and during the pass.,b:Blow your horn and pass closely.,c:Allow the motorcycle a full lane and do not crowd it.,d:Pass on the shoulder if the lane is narrow.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other vehicle.
