When passing, move completely into the passing lane, give the motorcycle plenty of space, and never crowd or share the lane with it. Only return to your lane after you can see the motorcycle clearly in your rearview mirror.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down, look carefully in all directions, and proceed only when it is safe. Treat it as a warning that cross traffic or pedestrians may be present.

question: What must you do when you approach an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,b:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and go when safe.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing mid-street, how should you respond?
options: a:You must stop for them.,b:You do not have to stop.,c:Honk and proceed.,d:Drive around them slowly.
note: Drivers must always exercise due care to avoid hitting pedestrians, even if the pedestrians are crossing illegally. If people are in the roadway, you must slow or stop as needed so they can cross safely, rather than trying to force your way through.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow signal indicate?
options: a:The protected left turn is about to end.,b:Yield to pedestrians only.,c:Stop and wait.,d:Left turns are prohibited.
note: A yellow left-turn arrow warns that your protected left-turn phase is ending. You should be prepared to stop if you have not yet entered the intersection, and understand that you will soon need to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians when the signal changes.

question: When in a work zone, what following distance practice should you follow?
options: a:Follow closely to the driver ahead.,b:Avoid tailgating and maintain a safe following distance.,c:Pass as soon as possible.,d:Ride the bumper to prevent merging.
note: Work zones often have sudden stops, lane shifts, and workers or equipment near the roadway. You should avoid tailgating and leave extra space between you and the vehicle ahead so you have more time to react to unexpected changes.

question: How must you yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle using siren and flashing lights?
options: a:Stopping immediately, even if you are within an intersection.,b:Drive as closely to the right edge of the road as possible and stop.,c:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using siren and flashing lights, you must yield the right‑of‑way by moving as far to the right side of the road as you safely can and stopping. Do not stop in an intersection; instead, clear the intersection first, then pull to the right and stop. Remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed and it is safe to reenter traffic.

question: What does a flashing red traffic light at an intersection require you to do?
options: a:The same thing as a yield sign.,b:The light is about to turn green.,c:The same thing as a stop sign.
note: A flashing red traffic light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, then look for other vehicles and pedestrians. Proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe to do so.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means what?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken line.,b:Passing is not permitted from either lane.,c:Passing is permitted only from the lane next to the solid line.,d:Both lanes may pass anytime.
note: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. Passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line and only when it is safe. Vehicles next to the solid yellow line may not cross it to pass.

question: If you encounter a flooded roadway, what is the safest action?
options: a:Slam on the brakes.,b:Turn around and find another route.,c:Drive only in the center of the roadway.
note: If you encounter a flooded roadway, do not try to drive through the water. Even shallow water can hide road damage or sweep a vehicle away. The safest choice is to turn around and use another route, even if it takes more time.

question: Is it legal to have open alcoholic containers in a vehicle on a highway?
options: a:Legal if only passengers drink.,b:Illegal to possess or drink from open containers in a vehicle.,c:Legal if the driver is not drunk.,d:Legal when parked on the shoulder.
note: Open container laws generally prohibit drivers and passengers from possessing or consuming alcohol from open containers in a vehicle being driven on a public road. In Maryland, it is illegal to have an open alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a motor vehicle while it is on a highway, regardless of whether the driver is drinking.

question: Which factor affects how alcohol is absorbed into the body?
options: a:Weight,b:Height,c:Intelligence
note: Body weight is one of the main factors that affects how quickly alcohol is absorbed and how strongly it affects you. People with lower body weight generally reach a higher blood alcohol concentration (BAC) from the same amount of alcohol than heavier people. Other factors include biological sex, how much and how quickly you drink, and whether you have food in your stomach.

question: Why avoid sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?
options: a:They require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.,b:Small vehicles cannot see trucks in rearview mirrors.,c:Large vehicles travel faster.,d:They can swerve more quickly.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than passenger cars and need a longer distance to stop, even with good brakes. If you stop suddenly in front of them, they may not be able to slow or stop in time to avoid a rear-end collision. Always leave extra space in front of large vehicles and avoid cutting in and braking hard.

question: What do yellow centerlines on the pavement indicate?
options: a:All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads. A solid yellow line generally means no passing, while a broken yellow line means you may pass when it is safe and legal. White lines, not yellow, are used to separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, such as on one-way streets or carpool lanes.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what is the correct immediate response?
options: a:Apply the brake and hold it.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly and use the brakes lightly.,c:Pull over quickly.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly to keep control and steer straight. Do not slam on the brakes. Ease your foot off the accelerator, let the vehicle slow down gradually, and then brake gently if needed. Once you have the vehicle under control and your speed is reduced, move safely to the side of the road.

question: What is the only thing that can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drinking caffeine.,b:Eating foods high in fat.,c:Time.
note: Only time lowers your blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Your body needs time to metabolize alcohol, and nothing—coffee, cold showers, exercise, or food—can speed this process up. You may feel more awake with caffeine or food, but you will still be impaired until enough time has passed for your BAC to drop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road, what should you be sure to do?
options: a:Flash your headlights as you pass.,b:Sound your horn as you pass.,c:Judge the distance and speed of any oncoming vehicles.
note: On a two-lane road, only pass when you are sure there is enough clear distance ahead and that oncoming vehicles are far enough away and not approaching too fast. If you are unsure about the speed or distance of oncoming traffic, do not start to pass.

question: When you come to a flashing red traffic light, what must you do?
options: a:You are traveling in the wrong direction.,b:You may not proceed until it changes to green.,c:Treat the intersection as if there is a stop sign.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to pedestrians and other vehicles in or approaching the intersection, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: If your vehicle's wheels have run off the pavement edge, what is the correct first action?
options: a:Turn the front wheels sharply to the left to get back on the pavement.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and gently apply the brakes.,c:Turn the front wheels slightly to the left to edge the car back onto the pavement.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, ease off the accelerator, and brake gently to slow down. Once the vehicle is under control and traffic allows, steer back onto the pavement gradually rather than jerking the wheel.

question: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, what should you do?
options: a:Steer to the right.,b:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.,c:Steer to the left.
note: In a rear-wheel skid, take your foot off the brake and accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. If the rear of the vehicle slides left, steer left to help straighten the vehicle and regain traction.

question: What should you do when roads are slippery after rain begins?
options: a:Avoid fast turns and stops.,b:Decrease look-ahead distance.,c:Test tires' traction by accelerating uphill.,d:Increase speed to shorten travel time.
note: When rain first begins, oil and dirt on the road make the surface very slippery. Slow down and avoid fast or sudden turns and stops so your tires can maintain traction and you reduce the chance of skidding.

question: When should you not use your horn?
options: a:To warn someone you might hit.,b:Near blind pedestrians.,c:When visibility ahead is limited.,d:To alert drivers of a danger.
note: Use your horn only to help prevent a collision or alert others to a real danger. You should not use your horn around blind pedestrians because they rely heavily on sound cues to orient themselves, and an unnecessary horn blast can be confusing or disorienting. Instead, slow down, yield, and proceed only when it is clearly safe.

question: What does 'implied consent' require of drivers in Maryland?
options: a:You will submit to a physical examination before licensure.,b:You will submit to a field sobriety test to determine impairment.,c:You must submit to a requested chemical test to determine your BAC.
note: Implied consent means that by driving on Maryland roads, you have already agreed to take a chemical test (such as a breath or blood test) if a law enforcement officer lawfully requests it to determine your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) or presence of drugs. Refusing this test can lead to license suspension and other penalties, even if you are not convicted of DUI.

question: A driver who has been drinking is more likely to have which impairment?
options: a:Yield right-of-way to emergency vehicles.,b:Keep a three to four second following distance.,c:Slower reaction time.,d:Increased alertness.
note: Alcohol affects the brain and nervous system, slowing your reaction time and making it harder to respond quickly to hazards. Even small amounts of alcohol can delay how fast you brake, steer, or make decisions, which greatly increases your risk of a crash.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, what is a safe practice?
options: a:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.,b:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots along both sides, especially on the right, as well as in front and behind. To stay safe, avoid driving beside them for long periods. Either drop back or pass promptly and safely so the truck driver can see you and you are not trapped in a blind spot.

question: What should you do to prepare yourself and your vehicle before driving?
options: a:Adjust the seat to a reclining position.,b:Kick the tires.,c:Properly adjust your seat and mirrors.
note: Before driving, you should adjust your seat so you can reach the pedals and controls comfortably and maintain good control of the vehicle, and adjust your mirrors to minimize blind spots and maximize visibility. Also make sure everyone is properly buckled and the vehicle is legally registered and in safe operating condition.

question: When should you wear a seat belt while in a vehicle?
options: a:Only on long trips.,b:All the time.,c:Only on high-speed highways.,d:Only when driving at night.
note: Seat belts should be worn every time you are in a moving vehicle. Laws generally require drivers and front-seat passengers to be belted, and many states, including Maryland, require all occupants under a certain age to be properly restrained in any seat. Wearing a seat belt at all times greatly reduces the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:Motorcycles do not follow traffic rules.,b:They can stop much quicker than cars.,c:They brake more slowly than cars.,d:They are heavier than cars.
note: Motorcycles are lighter and can often stop more quickly than cars. If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or space to react if the motorcyclist brakes suddenly or swerves to avoid a hazard. Always leave extra following distance behind motorcycles to reduce the risk of a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a short entrance ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do before merging onto the interstate?
options: a:Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane on the interstate and then speed up to match traffic.,b:Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.,c:Speed up on the ramp and enter the interstate only after you have identified a safe gap in traffic.
note: On a short entrance ramp without an acceleration lane, you must judge traffic carefully and wait for a safe gap before merging. Signal early, look for a suitable opening, and then accelerate firmly on the ramp so that you are close to the speed of traffic as you merge. Never use the shoulder as a makeshift acceleration lane, and do not force your way into traffic without a safe gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane when:
options: a:You are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,d:The other driver signals you to move back into the lane.
note: After passing, you should not move back into your original lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space ahead of that vehicle to return without cutting them off or forcing them to brake suddenly.

question: At what speed should you travel under varying conditions?
options: a:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.,b:At the speed limit.,c:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.
note: You must always adjust your speed to match road, weather, and traffic conditions, even if that means driving below the posted speed limit. In rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor visibility, a slower speed may be necessary to maintain control and stop safely, but you must never exceed the posted limit.

question: Which of these substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:All of the above.
note: Many substances can impair driving, including prescription drugs, over‑the‑counter medicines, and illegal drugs. Tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, and some cough or cold medicines with codeine or antihistamines can cause drowsiness, slow reaction time, and affect judgment. Because all of the listed options can impair driving, the correct choice is that all of the above can affect your ability to drive safely.

question: What should you do when driving on a slippery surface such as snow or ice?
options: a:Increase your following distance and avoid sudden braking or acceleration.,b:Pump your brakes rapidly to stop as quickly as possible.,c:Shift to a low gear before descending steep hills and brake gently.
note: On snow or ice, you should increase your following distance and avoid sudden braking or acceleration. Driving smoothly gives your tires the best chance of maintaining traction. Pumping the brakes rapidly is not recommended, especially in vehicles with ABS, and while shifting to a lower gear on steep hills can help, the most important general practice on any slippery surface is to leave extra space and avoid sudden inputs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To safely enter a gap in highway traffic, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.,b:Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead and the gap.,c:Speed up and let other vehicles make way.
note: To merge safely into highway traffic, you must be aware of vehicles behind and beside you as well as the traffic in the lane you are entering. Check behind you and your blind spots, then focus on the traffic in front and the size of the gap so you can adjust your speed to match the flow and enter smoothly. Never rely on other drivers to move out of your way by speeding up aggressively.

question: When must you obey a school crossing guard's directions?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only during school hours.,c:Only when children are present.
note: A school crossing guard has legal authority to direct traffic, similar to a traffic control device. You must obey the guard’s instructions whenever they are giving directions, regardless of the time of day or whether you see children present. Ignoring a crossing guard’s signal is both unsafe and against the law.

question: What do double yellow centerline markings indicate about passing?
options: a:Allowed from both directions.,b:Allowed only from your direction.,c:Not allowed from either direction.
note: A solid double yellow centerline means traffic in both directions is separated and passing across the lines is not allowed for either direction. You may cross these lines only when making a permitted left turn or when instructed by law enforcement, but you may not use the opposing lane to pass another vehicle.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:You should speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.,b:You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.,c:You should prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning phase is ending. You should prepare to stop if it is safe to do so and be ready to yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning. Do not speed up to beat the light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to exit the interstate, when should you start slowing?
options: a:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,b:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,c:As you approach the deceleration lane.,d:Before you see the exit sign.
note: On interstates, you should maintain highway speed until you reach the deceleration lane. Once you enter the deceleration lane, begin slowing to the posted exit or ramp advisory speed. Slowing early on the main travel lanes can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips along the roadway?
options: a:Alert inattentive drivers through vibration and sound.,b:Test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,c:Warn drivers of tire problems.,d:Provide decorative road texture.
note: Rumble strips are raised or grooved patterns on the roadway that cause vibration and noise when driven over. They are designed to alert inattentive or drowsy drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a hazard, such as an intersection, toll plaza, or work zone.

question: If your car's suspension is worn, what problem can result?
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Slack in the steering.
note: A worn suspension system can reduce your ability to control the vehicle, especially when turning, braking, or driving over bumps. This can lead to swaying, bouncing, and longer stopping distances, all of which increase the risk of losing control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering an intersection, in what order should you scan for traffic?
options: a:Look to your right.,b:Look to your left.,c:Look left, then right, then left again.
note: Before entering an intersection, scan left, then right, then left again. Traffic from the left is usually closer and reaches you first, so you double-check that direction. Also check straight ahead for vehicles, pedestrians, and any hazards before proceeding.

question: Which driving behavior most blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision scene.,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.
note: Slowing down just to look at a crash or incident, called rubbernecking, suddenly disrupts traffic speed and attention. This creates shock waves of braking behind you, increases congestion, and raises the risk of rear-end collisions. Choosing steady, predictable driving and avoiding distractions helps traffic flow smoothly.

question: When is it appropriate to sound your horn?
options: a:Another driver makes a mistake.,b:Another vehicle is in your way.,c:When it may help prevent a collision.
note: The horn is a safety device used to warn others of a possible collision, such as when someone is about to move into your lane or doesn’t see you. It should not be used to show anger or just because someone inconvenienced you. Use it briefly and only when it can help prevent a crash.

question: In heavy fog, what is the correct approach to driving?
options: a:Turn on high beam headlights.,b:Increase your speed so you clear the fog quickly.,c:Slow down and use low beam headlights.
note: In fog, high beams reflect off the water droplets and make it harder to see. You should slow down, turn on low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped), and increase following distance. If visibility is so poor that you cannot safely continue, pull completely off the roadway and wait until conditions improve.

question: What does a curb painted red indicate?
options: a:A loading zone.,b:Reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,c:No parking, standing, or stopping.
note: A red curb means you may not stop, stand, or park there for any reason, not even to quickly drop off or pick up passengers. This keeps certain areas clear for safety, such as near fire hydrants, intersections, or other critical zones.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when a crossing guard is present.,b:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,c:At all times.
note: Pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog must be given the right-of-way at all times.

question: If you encounter a deep puddle ahead, what is the best action?
options: a:Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.,b:Avoid the puddle if possible.,c:Maintain the posted speed to make it through the water.
note: Avoid driving through deep puddles whenever you can. Water can cause you to hydroplane, hide potholes or debris, and damage brakes or the engine. If you cannot avoid the water, slow down before entering and drive through at a low, steady speed.

question: When during rainy weather should you be most cautious about turning or stopping?
options: a:One half hour after it stops raining.,b:After it has been raining all day.,c:During the first half hour of rain.
note: During the first part of a rainstorm, oil and other residues on the road mix with the water and make the surface especially slick. This reduces traction, so you must be extra cautious when turning or stopping during the first 20–30 minutes of rain.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is your obligation to pedestrians at a crosswalk?
options: a:You must yield to pedestrians.,b:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles.,c:Construction workers must yield to you.,d:Pedestrians only yield when lights are present.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, whether they are marked or unmarked, and must stop when necessary to let them cross safely. Always approach crosswalks at a speed that allows you to stop if a pedestrian is present or about to enter.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what should you expect?
options: a:Slow down because the lane ends ahead.,b:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,c:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
note: Orange construction signs and cones mean you are entering a work zone. Expect workers, equipment, lane shifts, or closures ahead. Slow down, follow posted work-zone speed limits, and be prepared to stop or change lanes as directed.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is correct?
options: a:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.,b:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.,c:You should put on your cruise control near a railroad crossing to maintain a constant speed.
note: At railroad crossings, you must stop when a flagger, stop sign, or active warning device tells you to, and any time a train is approaching. Never assume you have the right-of-way over a train; always slow, look, and listen before crossing the tracks.

question: What should you do to avoid losing traction on wet roads?
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Slow down.
note: On wet roads, tires have less grip and can hydroplane, especially at higher speeds. Slowing down reduces the water buildup under your tires, helping them maintain contact with the road so you can steer and brake more safely.

question: How should you behave when approaching a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Carefully drive around them.,b:Honk as a warning and proceed.,c:Stop until the person is clear of your path.,d:Pass closely at low speed.
note: A white cane or guide dog indicates a blind or visually impaired pedestrian. You must stop and yield the right-of-way, allowing them to completely clear your lane and any nearby lanes they may enter before you proceed.

question: On a roadway marked with a single broken white centerline, what is permitted?
options: a:You must stay within your lane.,b:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes when it is safe, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling your intention.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer signals you to stop while the traffic signal is green, what should you do?
options: a:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.,b:Obey the traffic signal.,c:Obey the officer.
note: A police officer’s directions override traffic signals and signs. If an officer signals you to stop, you must stop even if the traffic light is green, and follow the officer’s instructions until they release you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is unsafe behavior on an interstate?
options: a:Slower traffic keeping to the right.,b:Changing lanes without signaling.,c:If you miss your exit, proceed to the next exit.
note: On interstates, it is unsafe and illegal in most places to change lanes without signaling because other drivers cannot anticipate your movement. You should signal every lane change, keep slower traffic to the right, and if you miss an exit, continue to the next one rather than making sudden or unsafe maneuvers.

question: At what speeds can a car begin to hydroplane on standing water?
options: a:40 miles per hour.,b:35 miles per hour.,c:45 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can start at relatively low highway speeds when there is enough standing water and your tires cannot push the water away. Around 35 mph, especially with worn tires or deeper water, your tires can begin to ride up on a thin film of water and lose contact with the road, greatly reducing steering and braking control.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:Alertness.,b:Coordination.,c:Both of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs slow your brain and body, which reduces alertness, coordination, reaction time, and judgment. Because both alertness and coordination are affected, your overall ability to notice hazards, steer smoothly, and react in time is seriously reduced, making driving unsafe even at low levels of impairment.

question: What does a red arrow pointing right on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.,b:Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.,c:Turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.
note: A steady red arrow means you must stop and you are not allowed to turn in the direction of the arrow. You must wait until a green arrow or green light appears before making the turn, and then proceed only when it is safe and legal to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Check blind spots by looking over your shoulder.,b:Change lanes or pass in an intersection.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,d:Signal your intent.
note: You should not change lanes or pass another vehicle within an intersection because traffic is crossing and paths are more complex, increasing the risk of a collision. When changing lanes, you should always signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check blind spots before moving into the new lane.

question: What do double solid yellow lane markings indicate?
options: a:Neither lane may pass.,b:Both lanes may pass.,c:The lane to the right may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines between lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions mean that passing is not allowed for vehicles in either direction. You must stay in your lane and may only cross these lines when making a permitted left turn or when directed by traffic control or emergency personnel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the best way to change lanes?
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:When a car is in your blind spot.,c:Gradually and carefully.
note: The safest way to change lanes is to do it gradually and carefully. Check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to clear your blind spot, signal in advance, and only move when there is a safe gap. Sudden or frequent lane changes increase the risk of a collision.

question: If an oncoming vehicle's bright headlights affect your vision at night, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the other driver passes.,b:Look below their headlights.,c:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.
note: When oncoming high beams affect your vision, do not look directly at the lights. Instead, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road to use it as a guide, while using your peripheral vision to track the other vehicle until it passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What approach should a driver take regarding right-of-way rules?
options: a:Assume all drivers obey right-of-way rules.,b:Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.,c:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way to avoid collisions.
note: Right-of-way rules say who should go first, but they do not guarantee that others will follow them. You should always be prepared to yield your legal right-of-way if it will help avoid a collision, even when you technically have the right to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to turn left on a red light?
options: a:When traveling on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street after stopping.,b:When on a two-way turning onto a two-way after stopping.,c:Whenever traffic is light.,d:Never under any circumstances.
note: In many U.S. states, after coming to a complete stop and yielding to traffic and pedestrians, you may turn left on red only when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street, unless a sign prohibits it. You may not turn left on red from a two-way street onto a two-way street.

question: If your car begins to skid, how should you react?
options: a:Pump the brakes.,b:Stay off the brakes and steer to regain control.,c:Apply maximum braking force.,d:Turn off the engine immediately.
note: If your car begins to skid, stay off the brakes and off the accelerator. Look and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, making smooth steering corrections until you regain traction. Hard braking or sudden inputs can make the skid worse.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?
options: a:Oncoming cars.,b:Overtaking cars.,c:No one.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians until it is safe to turn.

question: When driving on a dimly lit street at night, how should you drive?
options: a:Slow enough to stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.,b:Turn on your high beam headlights to better see ahead.,c:Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.
note: Drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the distance lit by your headlights so you can avoid hazards in time.

question: How should you follow a large truck on the freeway?
options: a:No more than one car length behind.,b:Farther behind than when following a passenger car.,c:Closely behind in bad weather.,d:Directly beside the truck.
note: Give extra following distance behind large trucks because they have larger blind spots and require more stopping distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left at an upcoming corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Only to oncoming vehicles also turning left.,b:To oncoming vehicles and pedestrians in the crosswalk.,c:To pedestrians who are crossing or have the Walk signal.
note: When you turn left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Oncoming traffic has the right‑of‑way unless they are controlled by a signal giving you a protected left turn. Never start your turn until you are sure all oncoming vehicles and pedestrians you might conflict with have cleared or are far enough away.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: May you drive off the paved roadway to pass another vehicle?
options: a:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:If there are two or more lanes in your direction.,d:If the shoulder is paved and wide.
note: You may not drive off the paved or main-traveled portion of the road (onto the shoulder) to pass another vehicle.

question: How do defensive drivers think about others on the road?
options: a:They know other drivers will do the right thing.,b:They consider what other drivers might do and are prepared to react.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.
note: Defensive drivers do not assume others will always follow the rules. Instead, they constantly think about what other drivers might do—especially mistakes—and stay ready to slow, stop, or change lanes safely. This mindset helps prevent crashes caused by someone else’s unexpected actions.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas around your vehicle that cannot be seen in your mirrors and require a head check.,b:Spots in your vision when tired.,c:Traffic control devices.,d:The rearview mirror view.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see using your mirrors alone. They are typically along the sides and slightly to the rear of your vehicle. Because vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles can hide in these areas, you must briefly turn your head to check over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and maintenance areas?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Red.,c:Orange.,d:Green.
note: In work zones, traffic control devices such as signs, cones, drums, and barriers are typically orange. Orange warns drivers that there are construction or maintenance activities ahead and that they should slow down, stay alert, and be prepared for lane shifts or workers on or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking downhill, how should you position your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.,b:Keep your wheels straight.,c:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.
note: When parking facing downhill, you should turn your front wheels toward the curb or roadside. If the vehicle starts to roll, it will move into the curb or edge of the road instead of into traffic. Always set the parking brake as well.

question: What can tailgating other drivers cause?
options: a:Reduce collisions.,b:Frustrate other drivers and increase danger.,c:Prevent passing.,d:Improve traffic flow.
note: Tailgating means following another vehicle too closely. It reduces your time to react if the driver ahead brakes or swerves and often makes other drivers nervous or angry, which can lead to sudden or unsafe maneuvers. Keeping a safe following distance lowers the risk of rear-end collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive markedly slower than surrounding traffic, what is likely to happen?
options: a:Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,b:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.,c:Improve traffic flow.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be just as dangerous as speeding. Other drivers may need to brake or change lanes suddenly to get around you, which increases the risk of crashes. If you are impeding the normal, safe flow of traffic without a good reason, you can be cited for obstructing traffic.

question: Before driving, how much of the vehicle's windows should you clear of snow, frost, and ice?
options: a:Just the windshield.,b:All windows.,c:Just the windshield and passenger window.
note: Before driving, you should clear snow, frost, and ice from all windows and mirrors so you have a full, unobstructed view in every direction. Limited visibility makes it harder to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and hazards, and in many states it is illegal to drive with windows that are not properly cleared.

question: When weather or reduced visibility requires headlights, which should you use?
options: a:Use your parking lights.,b:Use your high beams.,c:Use your low beams.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or other low-visibility conditions, you should use your low beam headlights. Low beams help you see the road and help others see you without causing glare. High beams can reflect off fog, rain, or snow and actually make it harder to see, and parking lights alone are not sufficient for driving.

question: As you approach the top of a hill, how should you drive?
options: a:Maintain a steady speed.,b:Prepare to stop if necessary.,c:Speed up slightly.,d:Move into the left lane.
note: As you approach the top of a hill, you cannot see what is on the other side, so you must be ready to stop if needed. Reduce speed and stay in your lane so you can react safely to stalled vehicles, slow traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards that may be just beyond the crest.

question: What is the typical color and shape of construction zone signs?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
note: Construction and work-zone signs are usually orange with black symbols or lettering and are often diamond-shaped, though some may be rectangular. The orange color warns drivers of temporary conditions such as road work, lane shifts, or workers and equipment near the roadway.

question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?
options: a:To see potential hazards earlier.,b:Because it takes a quarter-mile to stop.,c:Because it helps you keep up with traffic.
note: On freeways you travel at higher speeds, so situations develop and change more quickly. Looking farther ahead gives you more time to see slowing traffic, lane changes, and hazards early so you can react smoothly instead of braking or swerving at the last second.

question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?
options: a:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,b:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.,c:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.
note: Many drugs can affect your driving, including prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines such as cold or allergy pills. They can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, or slower reactions. Always read labels and follow medical advice; do not drive if a medication can affect your alertness or coordination.

question: To whom must you give the right-of-way when they are crossing the street?
options: a:Only if they are in a marked crosswalk.,b:Only pedestrians near traffic lights.,c:Pedestrians in any marked or unmarked crosswalk at an intersection, and you should be prepared to yield to pedestrians crossing any street when necessary for safety.
note: Drivers must yield the right‑of‑way to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks at intersections. An unmarked crosswalk exists at most intersections, even if there are no painted lines. You should also be prepared to yield to pedestrians crossing the street anywhere, especially if they are already in the roadway or may be in danger.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When the other driver signals you to return.,b:When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:After three seconds of signaling.,d:When you pass the other vehicle's front bumper.
note: When you pass, you must not move back too soon or you may cut off the other driver. It is generally safe to return to your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle (its headlights in the dark) in your inside rearview mirror, which shows you have enough space ahead of it.

question: When bicycles are ridden on roadways, they are legally considered what?
options: a:Hazards.,b:Dangerous.,c:Vehicles.
note: When bicycles are ridden on the roadway, they are legally considered vehicles. Bicyclists must obey traffic signs, signals, and lane markings, and motorists must treat them like any other vehicle by yielding when required and giving them enough space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time and the other vehicle is on your left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.
note: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way. If the other vehicle is on your left, that means you are on their right, so you may proceed first after stopping and ensuring it is safe.

question: At a railroad crossing, which precautions should you take?
options: a:Watch for multiple trains.,b:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings (school buses, trucks with hazardous materials).,c:Both of the above.
note: When approaching a railroad crossing, you must look and listen for trains in both directions and be prepared to stop. You should also watch for vehicles such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials, because they are required to stop at all railroad crossings.

question: Which describes defensive driving behavior?
options: a:Putting one car length between you and the car ahead.,b:Looking only at the car directly in front of you.,c:Keeping your eyes moving to scan for possible hazards.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road ahead, to the sides, and behind you so you can spot hazards early and react in time. Keeping your eyes moving and checking mirrors regularly is safer than focusing only on the car directly in front of you.

question: What defines a crosswalk?
options: a:An area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.,b:Another name for a four-way intersection.,c:An area designated for road construction workers.,d:Only marked white lines between sidewalks.
note: A crosswalk is the part of the roadway set aside for pedestrian crossing. It may be marked with painted lines or unmarked at an intersection, but in both cases pedestrians have specific right-of-way protections when crossing there.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another vehicle passes you in a no-passing zone, how should you react?
options: a:Pull off the road.,b:Maintain your speed and position.,c:Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the drive lane.
note: If another driver passes you in a no-passing zone, do not speed up or try to block them. Instead, slow slightly if needed and create space so the passing vehicle can return to the lane safely, reducing the risk of a head-on collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving in the center lane of an expressway and are continually passed on both sides, what should you do?
options: a:Stay in the center lane.,b:Move to the lane on your right.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane expressways, the right lane is for slower traffic, the left lane is generally for passing, and the center lane is for through traffic moving at the normal speed of traffic. If you are in the center lane and vehicles are passing you on both sides, you are going slower than the flow. You should move safely to the right lane so faster traffic can pass on your left.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?
options: a:It occupies the driver's hands, eyes, and mind.,b:It draws attention of other drivers.,c:It costs money.,d:It improves communication while driving.
note: Cell phone use is dangerous because it creates manual, visual, and cognitive distraction. Your hands may leave the wheel, your eyes may leave the road to look at the phone, and your mind focuses on the conversation or screen instead of driving. This combination greatly increases the risk of a crash.

question: Which of the following is the correct way to operate the accelerator and brake pedals?
options: a:Use your left foot to brake.,b:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating your vehicle.,c:You should always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.
note: In normal passenger vehicles with automatic transmissions, you should use your right foot for both the accelerator and the brake. This helps prevent pressing both pedals at once and gives you consistent control. Apply the brakes smoothly and gradually, increasing pressure as needed for a controlled stop rather than braking abruptly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle traveling in the same direction, how should you pass?
options: a:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,b:Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.,c:Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.
note: When passing another vehicle, you should move into the passing lane, accelerate to pass safely, and complete the pass promptly without exceeding the speed limit. Lingering beside another vehicle creates blind-spot and collision risks. Return to your lane only when you can see the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and there is a safe following distance.

question: Signs with orange backgrounds are used to indicate what?
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Construction and maintenance warning signs.,c:General warning signs.
note: Orange background signs are used for temporary traffic control in construction and maintenance areas. They warn drivers about road work, lane shifts, reduced speeds, and workers or equipment on or near the roadway so drivers can slow down and proceed with extra caution.

question: When should you use your high-beam headlights while driving at night?
options: a:When there are no oncoming vehicles approaching.,b:When you are following another vehicle in heavy traffic.,c:When you are within a one-block distance of an oncoming vehicle.
note: Use high beams on dark, open roads when there are no oncoming vehicles and you are not close behind another vehicle. High beams help you see farther ahead, but they can blind other drivers. Dim to low beams at least about 500 feet before meeting oncoming traffic and when you are within a few hundred feet of a vehicle you are following.

question: When taking any medication, what should you do regarding driving?
options: a:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,b:Have someone follow you home.,c:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about effects before driving.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can make you drowsy, slow your reactions, or affect your judgment. Always check with your doctor or pharmacist about how a medication may affect your ability to drive before you get behind the wheel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian crosses your lane, what should you do?
options: a:Cautiously drive around them.,b:Make sure the pedestrian sees you then proceed.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,d:Honk and continue.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even where no marked crosswalk exists; stop and allow them to cross.

question: What is the crash risk effect of a BAC of 0.02 percent?
options: a:It won't affect your driving.,b:It won't put other drivers at risk.,c:It will nearly double your chances of having an accident.
note: Any amount of alcohol in your system can affect driving. Even at a BAC of about 0.02%, your judgment, visual functions, and ability to perform two tasks at once can be impaired, which increases your crash risk compared with sober driving. There is no safe BAC for driving; the only truly safe choice is not to drive after drinking.

question: When passing a line of parked cars, what should you be prepared for?
options: a:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.,b:Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.,c:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to allow more room for moving traffic.
note: When driving past parked cars, be ready for doors to open, people to step out from between vehicles, or a car to pull out suddenly. Slow down, leave extra space from the parked cars, and be prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under which condition may you pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a hill or curve.,b:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken line next to your lane means you may pass if it is safe and legal to do so. A solid line next to your lane or limited visibility on hills and curves means passing is prohibited because you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic.

question: What action will cause the MVA to suspend a driver's license related to testing?
options: a:Refusing to submit to a BAC or drug test.,b:Submitting to a breath test.,c:Using a fake ID to buy alcohol.,d:Failing a field sobriety test only.
note: Under implied consent laws, by driving you agree to take a chemical test (breath, blood, or urine) if lawfully requested. Refusing this test results in an automatic license suspension by the motor vehicle agency, even if you are never convicted of DUI.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, how should you wear it?
options: a:Only the lap belt.,b:Both the lap and shoulder belts.,c:Only the shoulder belt.,d:None if airbags are present.
note: In a two-part belt system, always wear both the lap and shoulder belts. The lap belt should be low and snug across the hips, and the shoulder belt should cross the chest and shoulder, not the neck or under the arm. Using only one part greatly reduces protection in a crash.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do about the brakes?
options: a:Brake abruptly.,b:Stay off the brakes.,c:Brake lightly.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. If you need to use the brakes and your vehicle does not have ABS, brake gently to avoid locking the wheels. With ABS, apply firm, steady pressure and let the system pump for you. Abrupt braking usually makes a skid worse.

question: As you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before crossing the intersection.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you to slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to yield to pedestrians and cross traffic that has the right-of-way.

question: When are large trucks likely to lose speed?
options: a:Driving up long or steep hills.,b:Driving down long, gradual hills.,c:Driving in long gradual curves.,d:Driving on level surfaces.
note: Large trucks are heavy and their engines must work harder when climbing long or steep hills. As the grade gets steeper, they often cannot maintain speed like smaller vehicles, so they slow down. You should anticipate this, avoid tailgating, and give trucks extra space when approaching or following them uphill.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is not working, what should you do at the intersection?
options: a:If the intersection is clear, you may not need to stop.,b:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.,c:Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.
note: When a traffic signal is completely out, the intersection must be treated as an all-way stop. You must come to a complete stop, then proceed only when it is safe, yielding to vehicles that arrived first, to vehicles on your right if you arrive at the same time, and to pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: Why should you look far ahead while driving on the highway?
options: a:Helps you keep up with traffic.,b:Reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.,c:Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.
note: Looking far ahead on the highway lets you see problems early, such as slowing traffic, lane closures, or debris. This extra time to react means you can brake or change lanes smoothly instead of making sudden, last‑second moves that can cause crashes or surprise drivers behind you.

question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead.,b:Toward the right, toward the side of the road.,c:Toward the left, toward the center of the road.
note: When parking uphill with no curb on a two-way road, turn your front wheels toward the right, toward the edge of the road. If the vehicle rolls, it will move off the roadway instead of into oncoming traffic, reducing the chance of a collision.

question: Which is a dangerous habit when driving in work zones?
options: a:Tailgating another vehicle.,b:Failing to watch for workers and moving equipment.,c:Both of the above.
note: Work zones are tight areas with changing traffic patterns, workers on foot, and construction equipment. Tailgating leaves you no room to react if traffic stops suddenly, and failing to watch for workers or machinery can lead to serious crashes. Safe drivers slow down, increase following distance, and stay alert for workers and equipment.

question: Which statement best describes backing up a vehicle?
options: a:Always dangerous.,b:Dangerous if you have a helper.,c:Only dangerous in large vehicles.
note: Backing up is always risky because your view is limited and it’s harder to see people, objects, or traffic behind you. You should back slowly, check mirrors, look over your shoulder, and use a helper when possible to reduce—but not remove—the danger.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, you should:
options: a:Quickly swerve into the next lane.,b:Speed up to scare them away.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: Animals near the road can move suddenly into your path. Slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop. Do not swerve or speed up, as that can cause you to lose control or collide with another vehicle.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Blind spots are eliminated with one outside mirror.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked by looking in the rearview mirror.,d:Blind spots do not exist on modern vehicles.
note: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot fully cover. Large trucks and buses have much larger blind zones along the sides, front, and rear, so you should avoid lingering next to or close behind them.

question: When is it necessary to use your low beam headlights?
options: a:On a lighted street.,b:On a freeway.,c:In fog.
note: In fog you must use low beam headlights because high beams reflect off the moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Use low beams in any condition with reduced visibility, such as fog, heavy rain, or snow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, to whom should you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your left.,b:Anyone who arrived before you.,c:The driver across from your vehicle.
note: At a four-way stop, drivers proceed in the order they arrive. You must yield to any vehicle that reached the intersection before you. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what should you do first?
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.,c:Wait until it is safe, then gradually re-enter the roadway.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and avoid jerking the vehicle back onto the road. Once you’ve slowed and checked for traffic, gently steer back onto the pavement when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to enter a freeway but see no gap in traffic, what should you do on the ramp?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.,b:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.
note: Use the ramp to adjust your speed so you can merge smoothly into freeway traffic. If there is no gap, slow down on the ramp and wait for a safe opening; avoid stopping at the end of the ramp unless absolutely necessary, and never force other drivers to brake or swerve.

question: Which type of road surface tends to freeze first?
options: a:A tunnel.,b:An intersection.,c:A bridge.
note: Bridges and overpasses freeze first because cold air surrounds them from above and below, cooling the surface faster than regular roadways that sit on the ground. Even when nearby pavement looks wet, a bridge can be icy.

question: What is considered a distraction while driving?
options: a:Anything that makes you pay more attention to driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Only cell phone use.,d:Only passengers making noise.
note: A distraction is anything that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving. This includes phones, eating, adjusting controls, or interacting with passengers—anything that reduces your focus on driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a curb, what should you do?
options: a:Drive more slowly than traffic for 200 feet.,b:Wait for a large enough gap to reach the speed of traffic.,c:Pull directly into the first available gap.,d:Stop and back into traffic if needed.
note: When pulling out from a curb, wait for a gap that lets you accelerate smoothly up to the speed of traffic without forcing others to slow or change lanes. Signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and merge only when you can match the flow safely.

question: What color and lettering do temporary construction and maintenance signs use?
options: a:Red background with green writing.,b:Orange background with black writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.
note: Temporary construction and maintenance (work zone) signs are standardized with an orange background and black lettering or symbols. The bright orange color alerts drivers to changing road conditions, workers, and equipment ahead so they can slow down and proceed with extra caution.

question: When parking on any hill, which practice should you follow?
options: a:One rear wheel should touch the curb.,b:Use the parking brake and leave the car in park.,c:Leave the front wheels parallel to the road if a curb exists.,d:Leave the vehicle in neutral.
note: When parking on any hill, you should always set the parking brake and leave the vehicle in Park (or in gear for a manual transmission). This helps prevent the vehicle from rolling if the primary parking mechanism fails. In addition, you should turn your wheels appropriately for the direction of the slope and presence of a curb, but using the parking brake and Park/gear is the universal rule.

question: When following a motorcycle, how should you adjust your following distance?
options: a:Be ready to use your horn.,b:Drive more slowly.,c:Allow a larger following distance.
note: Motorcycles are smaller, harder to see, and can stop or swerve more quickly than larger vehicles. You should allow a larger following distance—at least three to four seconds—so you have enough time to react if the motorcyclist slows, stops, or swerves to avoid road hazards.

question: How can you avoid headlight glare from an approaching car?
options: a:Look briefly toward the right side of the road.,b:Keep focused on the centerline.,c:Flash your high beams.,d:Stare straight ahead.
note: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, briefly look toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road while still keeping track of your lane position. This helps protect your night vision and prevents you from being temporarily blinded, while still allowing you to drive safely within your lane.

question: When driving at night, what should you do to improve safety?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night your visibility is reduced and it is harder to judge speed and distance, so you should increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react. Use high beams only when there is no oncoming traffic and no vehicle directly ahead of you, and never look directly into oncoming headlights to avoid being blinded.

question: When must you present proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.
note: You must carry proof of financial responsibility (usually an insurance card) and show it to a law enforcement officer any time they lawfully request it, such as when you are stopped for a citation or involved in a collision.

question: As your speed increases, what becomes more important?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Look well ahead of your vehicle.,c:Change lanes frequently.
note: At higher speeds you cover more distance in less time, so you must look farther ahead to detect hazards early and give yourself enough time and space to react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an octagonal (eight-sided) sign, what must you do?
options: a:Turn.,b:Stop.,c:Slow.
note: An octagonal (eight‑sided) sign is always a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop at the limit line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, yield as needed, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,b:Scanning the environment and staying focused on the driving task.,c:Exceeding the posted speed limit and driving too fast for conditions or circumstances.
note: Driving faster than the posted speed limit or too fast for weather, traffic, or road conditions greatly increases your stopping distance and crash risk, making speeding a common contributing factor in collisions.

question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?
options: a:Maintain your normal speed.,b:Increase speed to clear the zone quickly.,c:Reduce speed and be prepared to stop.,d:Ignore lane markings in the zone.
note: In work zones you must slow down, obey all posted work‑zone speed limits and signs, and be prepared to stop because workers, lane shifts, and equipment can appear unexpectedly.

question: What can you do to help reduce road rage incidents?
options: a:Always signal your intention when changing lanes.,b:Use your horn frequently.,c:Talk on your cell phone while driving.
note: Signaling your intentions, following traffic laws, and staying courteous helps prevent misunderstandings that can trigger road rage. Avoid aggressive gestures, tailgating, or using your horn unnecessarily, and give other drivers space to correct mistakes.

question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you and creates a hazard. What should you do first?
options: a:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Swerve into the lane next to you.
note: When a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, the safest first response is to ease off the accelerator. This gently increases your following distance without the risk of skidding or being rear‑ended. Brake more firmly only if needed, and avoid sudden swerves that could cause a collision in another lane.

question: How can you help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away?
options: a:Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,b:Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.,c:Maintaining a steady speed.
note: Maintaining a steady speed and signaling early helps drivers behind you judge their following distance and react smoothly. Frequent speed changes or sudden braking can surprise the driver behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

question: What is hydroplaning?
options: a:The windshield wipers cannot keep the windshield clear of rain.,b:Tires lose contact with the road surface.,c:Spray from a large truck reduces visibility.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride up on a layer of water and lose direct contact with the road. This can cause a partial or total loss of steering and braking control. To reduce the risk, slow down in heavy rain, avoid standing water, and make sure your tires have good tread.

question: Which statement about driving through roadwork zones is true?
options: a:Fines are the same for violations in work zones as under normal conditions.,b:You must "Slow for the Cone Zone.",c:Only slow down if you think workers are present.
note: In work zones you must slow down, obey posted signs, and be prepared for sudden stops or lane shifts. Many states increase fines for violations in marked work zones, especially when workers are present, which is why you are reminded to “Slow for the Cone Zone.”

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, you should be driving:
options: a:At the legal speed limit.,b:More slowly than the freeway traffic.,c:At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
note: When using a freeway on‑ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of freeway traffic (as long as it is safe and not above the speed limit). Entering much slower than other vehicles forces them to brake or swerve and increases the risk of a collision.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow when visibility is poor, what is a good way to let others know you are present?
options: a:Turn up the instrumental panel lights.,b:Turn on your parking lights.,c:Turn on your headlights.
note: In low‑visibility conditions such as dawn, dusk, rain, or snow, turn on your headlights (low beams). Headlights make your vehicle easier for others to see. Parking lights or instrument panel lights alone do not provide enough visibility or make you clearly visible to other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must drivers obey directions given by flaggers at road works?
options: a:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,b:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.,c:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
note: Flaggers in construction or work zones are authorized to control traffic. Their signals and directions must be obeyed just like traffic signs or signals, even if they differ from normal traffic controls, to protect workers and drivers.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is correct?
options: a:If you can walk in a straight line, it's safe to drive.,b:If under the legal BAC limit, your driving isn't impaired.,c:Alcohol affects judgment needed for safe driving.,d:Alcohol only impairs at high concentrations.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time and impairs judgment, coordination, and decision‑making needed for safe driving. Even small amounts can affect your ability to drive safely, so you can be impaired even if you are under the legal BAC limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check freeway traffic before entering?
options: a:Using your rearview mirror.,b:Using your rearview and side mirrors.,c:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
note: Before entering a freeway, use your side mirror and then look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to merge. This shoulder check lets you see vehicles in your blind spot that mirrors alone cannot show, helping you merge safely.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian walking along the road and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move over.,c:Keep driving at the same speed; the oncoming vehicle must yield.,d:Stop and wait until the roadway is completely clear.
note: When you have both a pedestrian on the side of the road and an oncoming vehicle, you should not try to squeeze between them. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first, then move over and pass the pedestrian only when you have enough clear space and it is safe.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:When it has been raining hard for several hours.,b:When they are clean and dry.,c:Just after it starts to rain.
note: Roads are most slippery just after it starts to rain because the water lifts oil, grease, and other residues to the surface, creating a slick film. After it has rained for a while, much of this buildup is washed away and traction usually improves.

question: When following another vehicle at night, which headlights should you use?
options: a:High beams.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beams.,d:Fog lights.
note: When you are following another vehicle at night, use low beam headlights so you do not shine bright light into the driver’s mirrors and reduce their ability to see. High beams are for open road use when there is no vehicle directly ahead of you or coming toward you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you check for vehicles in your blind spots?
options: a:The inside rearview mirror.,b:The outside rearview mirror.,c:By looking over your shoulder.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot cover. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to make sure there is no vehicle in your blind spot.

question: If poor weather reduces your visibility, what should you do regarding following distance?
options: a:Speed up to get off the road quickly.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: In poor weather or any situation with reduced visibility, you should increase your following distance. More space gives you extra time to see hazards and react smoothly if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

question: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, when may vehicles behind it proceed?
options: a:When all students are off the bus.,b:When the stop arm is retracted.,c:When the stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
note: When a school bus has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must remain stopped. Do not move again until the red lights are off, the stop arm is fully retracted, the bus has started moving, and you are sure no children are in the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your original lane after passing, what should you confirm?
options: a:Beep your horn.,b:See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:Flash your headlights.
note: After passing, only return to your original lane when you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror and you have enough space to move back without cutting them off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it acceptable to start across an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.,c:Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space for your vehicle to completely clear it, regardless of the light color when you enter. If you would end up stopped in the intersection and blocking cross traffic when the light changes, you must wait behind the stop line until you can fully clear the intersection.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Call your insurance company when you get home.,b:Wait for the owner to return.,c:Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you must leave a note in a secure, visible place on the vehicle with your name, address, and contact information, and report the collision to authorities if required by state law.

question: How should you change speed and direction on snowy or icy roads?
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,b:Make speed and directional changes more gradually.,c:Drive as you would on dry pavement.,d:Brake suddenly to test traction.
note: On snowy or icy roads, reduce speed and make all changes—accelerating, braking, and steering—slowly and smoothly. Sudden movements can cause skids, and cruise control should not be used because it can make it harder to react to loss of traction.

question: What should you do if you become drowsy while driving?
options: a:Try to fight it and keep driving.,b:Take a break and rest.,c:Take caffeine pills and continue.,d:Drive with cruise control.
note: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should get off the road at the next safe place and rest or switch drivers. Fatigue greatly slows reaction time and can cause you to fall asleep briefly without realizing it. Caffeine or trying to fight sleep are not reliable or safe solutions.

question: What does a five-sided (pentagon) traffic sign indicate?
options: a:Stop sign.,b:Regulatory sign.,c:School zone or school crossing sign.
note: A five‑sided (pentagon) sign is used for school zones and school crossings. It warns drivers to slow down, watch for children, and be prepared to stop for pedestrians in or near the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If there's no marked crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and carefully pass.,b:Make eye contact then pass.,c:Stop and allow the pedestrian to finish crossing.,d:Honk to warn them.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing the road even where no crosswalk is marked; stop and allow them to cross safely.

question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signals?
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:When pulling next to the curb but not away.,c:When pulling next to or away from the curb.
note: You must signal any time you change your vehicle’s position on the road, including when pulling toward a curb to park and when leaving the curb to reenter traffic. Signaling lets other drivers and pedestrians anticipate your movement and avoid conflicts.

question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,b:Stop if you are driving in the same direction.,c:Stop, regardless of your direction of travel, unless the roadway is divided by a physical barrier or unpaved median that separates your lane from the bus.
note: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop whether you are approaching from behind or from the opposite direction, unless the roadway is divided by a physical barrier or unpaved median that separates your lane from the bus. Stopping protects children who may cross the road unexpectedly.

question: It is unsafe for a child under what age to ride in the front seat of a passenger vehicle?
note: Children under age 13 are safest riding properly restrained in the rear seat because front airbags deploy with great force and can seriously injure younger children. Always follow both state child-restraint laws and the vehicle/seat manufacturer’s instructions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the effect of continually passing vehicles on a two-lane road?
options: a:It increases your chances of a collision.,b:It helps prevent congestion.,c:Gets you more quickly and safely to your destination.,d:It is always legal.
note: On a two-lane, two‑way road, every pass puts you into the oncoming lane and increases your risk of a head‑on collision or sideswipe.
