Continually passing other vehicles greatly increases this risk; only pass when it is legal, necessary, and clearly safe, and be prepared to stay in your lane if conditions are not ideal.

question: What does a steady green traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Adjust your mirrors.,c:You may proceed through the intersection at a safe speed if it is clear.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if it is safe and legal, but you must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in the intersection or oncoming traffic when turning left.

question: What does the abbreviation 'BAC' mean?
options: a:Blood alcohol concentration.,b:Blood alcohol conservation.,c:Big alcohol content.
note: BAC stands for blood alcohol concentration and measures the percentage of alcohol in the bloodstream.

question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a two-lane street. What should you expect?
options: a:May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.,b:May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,c:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.
note: Large trucks often must swing wide to the left before turning right because their rear wheels track closer to the curb than the front wheels. Expect this wide turn, do not drive into the space they create on the right, and stay out of the truck’s blind spots.

question: What is the best response if you become tired while driving?
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window and keep driving.,c:Drink coffee and drive on.,d:Turn on loud music to stay awake.
note: If you feel tired while driving, the only safe choice is to stop and rest or switch drivers. Opening windows, turning up music, or drinking coffee may make you feel more alert for a short time, but they do not prevent drowsiness and greatly increase your crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Turn into any lane.,b:Turn into the first lane.,c:Turn into the second lane.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you must turn into the first available lane going your direction, usually the lane closest to the left curb. This keeps traffic organized and prevents conflicts with vehicles already in the other lanes.

question: If your car is equipped with airbags, what is the rule about seat belts?
options: a:Seat belts do not need to be worn.,b:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.,c:Seat belts should still be worn.
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. You must still wear your lap and shoulder belt properly so that, in a crash, the belt holds you in place and the airbag can cushion you safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes, besides checking your mirrors, what else should you do?
options: a:Never look over your right shoulder.,b:Always slow down in your traffic lane.,c:Glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you are moving to check your blind spot. This brief head check helps you see vehicles that mirrors cannot show.

question: What does a broken (dashed) yellow line between two lanes of traffic indicate?
options: a:Both lanes of traffic are going in the same direction.,b:Passing is permitted when it's safe.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken (dashed) yellow line between lanes means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when it is safe. You may cross the line to pass, but only if you can see far enough ahead and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: Why should you frequently check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Only when you are slowing down.,b:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.,c:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
note: You should check your mirrors often to stay aware of traffic behind and beside you so you can react early to hazards, lane changes, or vehicles approaching quickly. However, mirrors do not show your blind spots; you must also turn your head to check those areas.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Applying your brakes.,b:Letting go of the steering wheel.,c:Pressing your head against the head restraint.
note: If you are about to be hit from the rear, keep both hands firmly on the steering wheel to maintain control and press your head against the head restraint to reduce whiplash. Do not let go of the steering wheel.

question: What must you do when approaching a stopped school bus with flashing lights and an extended signal arm?
options: a:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are visible.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted.,c:Slow and pass carefully.,d:Honk and pass quickly.
note: When a school bus has flashing red lights and an extended stop arm, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted, and it is clear that children are no longer entering or leaving the bus.

question: A pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross as you make a right turn. What should you do?
options: a:Turn off your engine until the person crosses.,b:Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.,c:Wait until the person has crossed before turning.
note: A pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane is blind or visually impaired and always has the right-of-way. Stop and wait until the person has completely crossed and is safely out of your path before you turn.

question: What are "no zones" around large trucks?
options: a:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or limit the truck's ability to maneuver safely.,b:Places with plenty of room to follow a truck, c:Zones where several car lengths separate you from the truck.
note: “No zones” are the large blind spots and limited-maneuver areas around trucks and buses where your vehicle may not be visible to the driver or where the truck cannot stop or turn safely if you are too close.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate, after checking for a gap and signaling you should:
options: a:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed into the lane, since you have the right-of-way.,b:Wait for the lane to clear before merging.,c:Merge carefully into the gap.
note: On an interstate entrance ramp, you must find a safe gap, signal, accelerate to match the speed of traffic, and then merge carefully into the gap. Do not assume other drivers will move over or slow down for you; you are responsible for merging only when it is safe.

question: How can sudden wind gusts affect vehicles on highways?
options: a:They only affect large vehicles.,b:They can cause problems for all vehicles.,c:They only reduce visibility.,d:They only affect parked cars.
note: Sudden wind gusts can push any vehicle sideways, making it harder to stay in your lane and control steering. While large vehicles are especially affected, smaller vehicles and motorcycles can also be blown off course, and blowing dust or debris can reduce visibility for everyone.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drug use?
options: a:Alertness and concentration.,b:Reaction time and coordination.,c:All of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs affect multiple driving skills at once. They reduce alertness and concentration, slow your reaction time, and impair coordination, making it harder to steer, brake, and respond to hazards safely.

question: In traffic moving at 50–55 mph, how are you least likely to have an accident?
options: a:Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.,b:Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.,c:Stay within that speed range as other traffic does.
note: You are least likely to have a crash when you travel at the same general speed as surrounding traffic, as long as you stay within the posted speed limit. Large speed differences—either faster or slower than other vehicles—create more lane changes and conflicts, increasing collision risk.

question: What is an important step to take when making a turn?
options: a:Always move to the left lane.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Check traffic in all directions.
note: Before making any turn, you must check traffic in all directions: use your mirrors, check your blind spots, and look for oncoming vehicles, pedestrians, and cyclists. Only begin the turn when you are sure the path is clear and it is safe to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, what must you yield to?
options: a:Pedestrians and bicyclists crossing and traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Cars approaching from the left only.,c:Only vehicles, not pedestrians.,d:No one; you have the right-of-way.
note: At a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians and bicyclists in the crosswalks and to all traffic already circulating in the roundabout. Vehicles inside the roundabout have the right‑of‑way over entering traffic, and drivers must also stop for people legally crossing at the approaches.

question: If the centerline has one solid yellow and one broken yellow with the broken next to your lane, what does it mean?
options: a:You are in a no-pass zone.,b:You may pass from your lane if clear.,c:You may only make right turns.,d:You must stop before passing.
note: A centerline with one solid yellow and one broken yellow means passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line. If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may pass on the left when it is safe, with enough clear distance and no oncoming traffic. You may not pass if the solid line is on your side.

question: How many alcoholic drinks are required to begin affecting your driving ability?
options: a:One,b:Two,c:Three
note: Any amount of alcohol can begin to affect your judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Even one drink may impair your ability to drive safely, so the safest choice is not to drive after consuming any alcohol.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When can you safely move back into the right lane after passing a vehicle going the same direction?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the entire front (both headlights) of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, do not move back into the right lane until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle, including both headlights, in your rearview mirror. This helps ensure you have enough space and will not cut the other driver off. Always signal and check your blind spot before returning to the lane.

question: If a school bus ahead on your side of the road has red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.,b:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,c:Stop until the lights stop flashing.
note: When a school bus on your side of the road has red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted. This protects children who may be crossing the road. Some states also require stopping when the bus is on the opposite side, unless a physical median divides the roadway.

question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,b:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,c:When parked on a level roadway with no curb.
note: When you are parked on a hill or sloping driveway, you should turn your wheels so that if your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic (toward the curb or edge of the road). When you are waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light, you should keep your wheels pointed straight ahead so that if you are hit from behind, you are not pushed into oncoming traffic.

question: When is driving permitted under the influence of medication that impairs you?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If you don't feel drowsy.,c:If prescribed by a physician.,d:If it's over-the-counter.
note: You must never drive if any medication—prescription or over‑the‑counter—impairs your ability to drive safely. If a drug causes drowsiness, slowed reaction, blurred vision, or affects judgment, you are considered impaired and must not drive, even if a doctor prescribed it.

question: Which lights should drivers use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: In rain, fog, or snow, use low beam headlights so you can see the road and so others can see you. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can create glare that reduces visibility. Parking lights alone are not bright enough and are not a substitute for headlights while driving.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should drivers do?
options: a:Always stop whether a stop sign is present or not.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the street. You should slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop if they are in or near the crosswalk. You are only required to stop when there is a crossing guard, a stop sign, a red light, or children actually in the crosswalk.

question: How should you respond to an aggressive driver?
options: a:Challenge them.,b:Get out of their way.,c:Speed up to pass them.,d:Make obscene gestures.
note: When you encounter an aggressive driver, focus on staying safe and avoiding conflict. Safely move out of their way, allow them to pass, and do not make eye contact, gesture, or respond to their behavior. Engaging or challenging them can escalate the situation and increase the risk of a crash.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, what should you do?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent sliding.,b:Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.,c:Slow down gradually and avoid using the brakes.
note: When your vehicle hydroplanes, the tires lose contact with the road and ride on a thin layer of water. You should ease off the accelerator, keep the steering wheel straight, and slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking or sudden steering, because these can cause a skid. As your speed drops, the tires will regain traction.

question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicate?
options: a:A construction zone is ahead.,b:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,c:Passing is permitted when the way is clear.
note: A broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road means traffic in both directions may pass when it is safe. You must check for oncoming traffic, ensure there is enough clear distance to complete the pass, and return to your lane before coming close to any oncoming vehicle. If it is not clearly safe, you must not pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red light with a green arrow, when are you permitted to proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:You must first come to a complete stop.,b:You must wait until the light changes.,c:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear, you may go.
note: A green arrow is a protected turn signal. When you have a green arrow, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow if you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear, after yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection. You do not need to stop first unless required by a sign or other traffic control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn explicitly prohibited?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On or near any curve or hill.,c:On a straight road with clear view for 500 feet.
note: U‑turns are generally prohibited on or near curves or hills where you cannot be seen by oncoming traffic in time. Limited sight distance makes it dangerous for vehicles approaching from either direction. Only make a U‑turn where it is legal, safe, and you have a clear view of oncoming traffic for a sufficient distance.

question: If a school bus is stopped ahead loading or unloading children with lights flashing and stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop until all the children have left the bus.,b:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Change lanes, slow, and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, unless a specific state law clearly exempts your direction of travel (such as on some divided highways). Children may cross the road unexpectedly, so stay stopped and watch carefully until the bus’s signals are turned off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a funeral procession?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to vehicles in the procession.,b:Drive between procession vehicles.,c:Pass on the right at high speed.,d:Ignore the procession entirely.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to a properly identified funeral procession. Once the lead vehicle has lawfully entered an intersection, the rest of the procession is usually allowed to follow together, and other drivers must wait until all vehicles in the procession have passed, even if they have a green light. Never cut into, pass aggressively, or interfere with the procession.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles.,b:Wherever signs and/or pavement markings permit passing.,c:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles.
note: Only pass where signs and pavement markings indicate that passing is allowed, such as with a broken center line and no “No Passing Zone” signs. Even where it is allowed, you must also have enough clear distance ahead, good visibility, and no oncoming traffic to complete the pass safely. Never pass in intersections, on curves, or where your view is blocked.

question: Where is the safest place for children age 12 and under in a vehicle with airbags?
options: a:The bed of a pickup truck.,b:The front seat.,c:The back seat.,d:Standing on the floorboard.
note: Children age 12 and under are safest in the back seat, properly secured in an appropriate child safety seat or seat belt. Front airbags are designed for adults and can seriously injure or kill a child in a crash, especially if the child is unrestrained or in a rear-facing seat. Never let children ride in the bed of a pickup or stand in a moving vehicle.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic, what is true about passing?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the left.,b:Passing is permitted from the right.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. You must stay in your lane and may only cross these lines when making a permitted left turn or when directed by law enforcement, never to pass another moving vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you not do?
options: a:Back up on the road or shoulder.,b:Continue to the next exit.,c:Find an alternate route.,d:Proceed to the next crossroad.
note: If you miss your freeway exit, keep going to the next exit and then find a safe route back. Never back up on the freeway or shoulder; reversing in high-speed traffic is extremely dangerous and illegal in most places. It is always safer to continue forward and re-route than to try to correct a missed exit by backing up.

question: How should you follow a large truck on the roadway?
options: a:Closer than when following a passenger car.,b:Farther behind than when following a passenger car.,c:To the right to pass quickly.,d:Directly beside the truck's blind spot.
note: Large trucks need more time and distance to stop and have larger blind spots. You should follow them at a greater distance than a passenger car so you can see the road ahead and have enough space to react and brake safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what is the correct action?
options: a:Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.,b:Merge across two lanes at once.,c:Always stop before entering the highway.
note: When using an interstate on‑ramp, use the acceleration lane to build up speed to match the flow of traffic, choose a safe gap, signal, and merge smoothly. You should not stop in the acceleration lane unless traffic or an emergency forces you to.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, what should you not assume?
options: a:That the other driver will make space for you to return.,b:That signaling makes passing illegal.,c:That they will slow down.,d:That they will always keep speed constant.
note: When passing, never assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane. You are responsible for making sure there is enough clear space ahead and behind, and that you can complete the pass safely without relying on the other driver to change speed or position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate from an on-ramp, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and check for cars before entering.,b:Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.,c:Check for cars, increase speed to match the flow, and merge when safe.
note: When entering an interstate, check traffic, signal, and use the ramp and acceleration lane to increase your speed to match the flow of traffic. Merge when there is a safe gap. Do not stop on the ramp unless traffic is stopped or you have no other choice.

question: How can you reduce the chance of skidding on slippery surfaces?
options: a:Speed up before entering curves.,b:Shift to a higher gear going down steep hills.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.,d:Brake hard during the curve.
note: To reduce the chance of skidding on slippery roads, slow down before you enter curves and intersections and make all speed and direction changes gently. Sudden braking, accelerating, or sharp steering in a curve can cause your tires to lose traction and the vehicle to skid.

question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs?
options: a:To keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.,b:To inconvenience drivers.,c:To make drivers angry about delays.,d:To mark detours only.
note: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to separate traffic from construction areas, protect workers, and guide drivers safely through or around the work zone. You must slow down, follow the signs and devices, and stay out of the closed or hazardous areas.

question: A diamond-shaped road sign generally indicates what?
options: a:Stop.,b:Warning of special conditions or hazards ahead.,c:Yield.,d:Regulatory requirements.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings, so you can slow down and be prepared. They are usually yellow, or orange in work zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill, what should you do before entering the curve?
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before the curve.,b:Slow to the posted freeway speed limit.,c:Wait until you are in the curve to begin braking.
note: On a downhill, curving off-ramp, you should slow to a safe speed before you enter the curve. Braking hard while in the curve can cause skidding or loss of control, especially on a downgrade. Enter the curve at a speed that allows you to stay in your lane comfortably.

question: What is the best definition of distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: Distracted driving is anything that takes your attention away from driving—this can be your eyes, hands, or mind. Examples include texting, eating, adjusting controls, or focusing on passengers instead of the road. Any distraction increases your risk of a collision.

question: What should you do when driving at night to increase safety?
options: a:Always use your high beams.,b:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.,c:Increase your following distance.
note: At night, you should increase your following distance because reduced visibility makes it harder to judge speed and distance and to see hazards in time. Leaving more space gives you extra time to react and stop safely if the vehicle ahead slows or stops.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem on the road, what should you do?
options: a:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.,b:Signal and pull into the slow lane.,c:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.
note: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem, signal, turn on your hazard lights, and move completely off the traveled portion of the road if possible. Stopping in a traffic lane is very dangerous because other drivers may not see you in time to avoid a collision.

question: If you are already inside an intersection when a green light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed so as not to cause an accident.,b:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,c:Stop immediately in the intersection.
note: A yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should continue through and clear the intersection safely. Stopping in the middle of the intersection can confuse other drivers and increase the risk of a crash.

question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Relax and concentrate on safe driving.,b:Tailgate slower drivers.,c:Drive above posted speed limits.,d:Honk repeatedly to move traffic.
note: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, stay calm, allow extra travel time, and focus on safe driving rather than on other drivers’ mistakes. Tailgating, speeding, and excessive honking are aggressive behaviors that increase the risk of crashes and can lead to road rage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:No one in particular.,c:Oncoming traffic should yield to you.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Only begin your turn when there is a safe gap in oncoming traffic and the crosswalk is clear.

question: If you are driving next to a single broken white line on a highway, what does it allow?
options: a:You cannot cross the line to pass.,b:You may cross the line to pass or change lanes.,c:You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.
note: A single broken (dashed) white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling your intention.

question: Which substance slows reaction time and impairs judgment leading to slower reactions?
options: a:Working hard.,b:Sleeping.,c:Drinking alcohol.,d:Caffeinated drinks.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows the central nervous system. It reduces alertness, slows reaction time, and impairs judgment about speed, distance, and hazards, which greatly increases the risk of a crash.

question: What does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Passing is permitted from both directions.,b:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: A dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means only the traffic on the side with the dashed line may cross the center line to pass when it is safe. Traffic on the side with the solid line must not cross to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check blind spots when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Only the left outside mirror.,b:Look over your left or right shoulder.,c:Only the inside rearview mirror.
note: Before changing lanes, you must briefly turn your head and look over the appropriate shoulder to check your blind spot. Mirrors alone cannot show vehicles that are alongside your car but not visible in the mirrors.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers.,d:Parking lights only.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights so the light aims down at the road. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and can bounce back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

question: A driver's license is legally considered which of the following?
options: a:A right you have automatically.,b:A privilege you must earn and maintain.,c:A mandatory requirement for all citizens.
note: Driving is not an automatic right; it is a privilege granted by the state. You must qualify for a license and follow traffic laws, and the license can be suspended or revoked if you violate those laws.

question: When driving in fog, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,b:Slow down and use your high beam headlights.,c:Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog because the light is aimed lower and creates less glare, helping you see the road and be seen by others. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. Always slow down, and if visibility is extremely poor, pull off the road to a safe place and wait until conditions improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection where your side view is blocked, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and look both ways.,b:Maintain your speed and look both ways.,c:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.
note: When your view is blocked at an intersection, you must treat it cautiously. Come to a complete stop if required, then move forward slowly until you can clearly see traffic in both directions. Only proceed when you are sure the way is clear. Simply slowing down without stopping may not give you enough time to react to cross traffic you cannot see.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving.,b:After driving a few minutes.,c:Whenever you think of it.,d:While the car is moving.
note: Adjust your seat, steering wheel, and all mirrors before you start driving so you have a clear view around your vehicle. This helps you avoid taking your attention off the road. Do not adjust mirrors while the car is moving, because it can distract you and increase the risk of a crash.

question: Which of the following is true about large trucks?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,c:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.
note: Large trucks are heavier and need much more distance to stop than passenger vehicles, especially when fully loaded or going downhill. They are also less maneuverable, and not all trucks have air brakes, and even air brakes do not make them stop quickly. Give trucks extra space and avoid cutting in front of them.

question: Which headlights should you use to improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or sleet, always use low beam headlights. Low beams cut through precipitation better and reduce glare. High beams can reflect off water droplets or fog and make it harder to see. Parking lights alone do not provide enough light and may not make your vehicle visible enough to others.

question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, which beam setting should you use?
options: a:High beams until 10 feet away.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.,d:Emergency flashers.
note: Use low beam headlights when you are following another vehicle at night so your lights do not shine directly into the driver’s mirrors and blind them. High beams are only for use when you are far enough away from other traffic that you will not interfere with other drivers’ vision.

question: When a traffic signal turns yellow as you approach, what should you do if you can stop safely?
options: a:Speed up to cross the intersection.,b:Slow down and proceed through the intersection without caution.,c:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. If you can stop safely before the intersection, you must do so. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through carefully, but you should never speed up to beat the red.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams at night, where should you direct your gaze?
options: a:Look straight ahead in your lane.,b:Look toward the left edge of your lane.,c:Look toward the right edge of your lane.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly at the glare. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane and use your peripheral vision to track the other vehicle. This reduces glare and helps you stay in your lane safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At intersections with a Yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is near enough to cause conflict.,b:Yield only to vehicles on your right.,c:Always slow down but never stop.
note: At a Yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Yield the right‑of‑way to any pedestrians and to vehicles in or close enough to the intersection that they would be a hazard if you entered. Proceed only when it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

question: Collisions are more likely to occur under which condition?
options: a:All vehicles traveling at roughly the same speed.,b:One lane of traffic traveling faster than the other lanes.,c:One vehicle moving faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
note: Collisions are more likely when one vehicle is moving much faster or much slower than surrounding traffic. Large speed differences create more passing, lane changes, and sudden braking, which increase the chance of crashes. It is generally safer when vehicles travel at similar speeds within the posted limit.

question: What is a common effect of excessive speed?
options: a:Increases ability to react.,b:Often leads to high-risk decision-making.,c:Does not change crash risk.,d:Makes driving safer.
note: Excessive speed reduces the time you have to see hazards, make decisions, and stop safely. At higher speeds, small mistakes become serious crashes more easily, and drivers are more likely to make risky choices such as late braking or unsafe lane changes.

question: Why increase following distance behind large vehicles?
options: a:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,b:Because large vehicles travel faster.,c:Because of the vehicle's slipstream.,d:To prevent others from cutting in.
note: Large trucks and buses block your view of the road ahead and have large blind spots. By increasing your following distance, you can see more of the road around them, have more time to react, and leave extra space for safe stopping.

question: After stopping for a passing train, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Proceed when the gates stop moving.,b:Look for a second train and wait until all signals stop.,c:Cross the tracks as soon as the first train passes.,d:Back up if traffic blocks your way.
note: After a train passes, always check carefully for a second train on another track and wait until all warning lights stop flashing and gates are fully raised. Only proceed when you are sure the tracks are clear in both directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Only when it helps prevent collisions.,b:Whenever it helps prevent collisions.,c:Never — it confuses other drivers.
note: Right-of-way rules help traffic flow, but safety comes first. You must be prepared to let another driver go, even if you have the legal right-of-way, whenever yielding will help prevent a collision. Never insist on your right-of-way if it would create a dangerous situation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Maryland's point system, the MVA will send a notice of license suspension if you accumulate how many points within a two-year period?
options: a:3 to 4 points,b:5 to 7 points,c:8 to 11 points,d:12 or more points
note: In Maryland, accumulating 8 to 11 points on your driving record within a two-year period will result in a license suspension notice from the MVA.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Maryland's point system, how many points accumulated within a two-year period will trigger a notice of license revocation?
options: a:8 points,b:10 points,c:12 or more points,d:6 points
note: Accumulating 12 or more points within a two-year period in Maryland will result in a notice of license revocation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are the minimum liability car insurance coverage limits required for all registered vehicles in Maryland?
note: Maryland law requires all registered motor vehicles to carry minimum liability insurance of 30/60/15: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, and $15,000 for property damage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Maryland GDL rules, a provisional license holder under age 18 is generally not permitted to drive unsupervised between what nighttime hours?
options: a:10:00 PM to 6:00 AM,b:11:00 PM to 5:00 AM,c:Midnight (12:00 AM) to 5:00 AM,d:Midnight (12:00 AM) to 6:00 AM
note: Maryland provisional license holders under age 18 are restricted from driving unsupervised between the hours of midnight and 5:00 AM, unless they have a valid employment or school-related exception.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When no speed limit is posted on a residential undivided highway in Maryland, what is the default legal speed limit?
options: a:25 mph,b:30 mph,c:35 mph,d:40 mph
note: Under Maryland law, the default (statutory) speed limit is 30 miles per hour on undivided highways in business and residential districts, unless a different limit is posted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under Maryland GDL rules, if a learner's permit applicant holds a valid out-of-country driver's license, how many hours of supervised practice driving must they complete?
options: a:60 hours (including 10 at night),b:30 hours (including 5 at night),c:14 hours (including 3 at night),d:No practice hours are required
note: If a Maryland learner's permit holder already holds a valid out-of-country driver's license, they must complete a minimum of 14 hours of supervised driving, with at least 3 of those hours completed at night.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How long must a rookie driver in Maryland hold a Learner's Instructional Permit without any traffic violations before they can graduate to a Provisional License?
options: a:3 months,b:6 months,c:9 months,d:12 months
note: Under Maryland's GDL program, rookie drivers must hold a Learner's Instructional Permit for a minimum of 9 months without any violations before they are eligible to apply for a provisional driver's license.
